Three controllable radiation nulls are introduced to achieve out-of-band suppression by loading cross-shaped patches, extending open-circuit branches, and designing special feeding networks, respectively. The measured −10 dB impedance bandwidth is 45% (3.3 GHz to 5.1 GHz), which covers the entire 5G bands of N77/N78/N79 bands. Meanwhile, the average in-band gain is 8.5 dBi, and the out-of-band suppression level is more than 15 dBi. A wideband filtering antenna array is designed for demonstration. The measured results show that the −10 dB impedance bandwidth is 45% (3.3 GHz to 5.1 GHz), and the average gain is 13 dBi with stable radiation characteristics within the whole band, which is a suitable choice for 5G base station applications.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Filtering Antenna Based on 3-D Printed Half-Mode Gap Waveguide Quadruple-Mode Resonator
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a high-selective dual-band filtering antenna for millimeter-wave application is first proposed based on a half-mode gap waveguide quadruple-mode resonator. Four resonant modes are simultaneously excited within a single cavity following the transversal hybrid electromagnetic coupling topology, thus forming dual-passband filtering characteristics. Three radiation nulls are generated on both sides of two passbands due to the created bypass coupling and can be controlled independently. A stacked radiating cavity with shared aperture provides uniform polarizations for dual-frequency application. For experimental validation, 3-D multijet printing technology was used to fabricate prototypes integrally, significantly reducing the assembly loss. The final measured results agreed well with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement Between Two Low-Profile Patch Antennas for In-Band Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An enhanced isolation technique between two low-profile patch antennas is proposed. Two identical antennas are configured with two printed circuit boards (PCBs) spaced at 0.206λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at 3.5 GHz. Every antenna is a rectangular patch with four slots and two vias, vertically fed with a coaxial probe. A decoupling strip embedded between two antennas and a slot on the ground improves isolation, which would not deteriorate the cross-polarization and backward radiation levels. Two-port impedance match and isolation characteristics are analyzed when the two-antenna spacing varies from 0.159λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 0.252λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The proposed antenna has a size of 0.817λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.448λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.038λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The fabricated prototype is measured, and the results demonstrate that the −10 dB impedance bandwidths are 3.37–3.61 GHz (6.88%), the port-to-port isolation is more than 45.2 dB, the realized gains are 4.53 ± 0.35 dBi, and the average radiation efficiencies are more than 70%. Therefore, the measured results agree well with the simulated, making it a promising candidate for in-band full-duplex applications in 5G terminal scenes.

articleTitle: An Aperiodic Subwavelength Dipole Structure for Enhancing Near-Field Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a sparse, aperiodic subwavelength dipole structure (ASDS) is proposed for enhancing wireless power transfer in the near field (NF). The ASDS can have applications in areas such as wireless charging of small electronics, imaging, and proximity sensing. The working principle is inspired by a shifted-beam NF focusing method for similar antenna structures, as well as previous examples of using loaded metawire arrays for far field beamforming. The ASDS is simulated for distances between 1<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda$</tex-math></inline-formula> and 3<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda$</tex-math></inline-formula> at 2.4 GHz in the industrial, scientific, and medical band. All dipole elements are parasitically excited by a single source dipole at the center. The design is numerically optimized by adjusting the dipoles' lengths and relative position; a figure of merit is proposed to quantify overall performance. Significant improvement in power transfer efficiency is obtained, compared to reference examples such as a uniformly excited array. The simplicity of the proposed ASDS also makes it advantageous, as no feed networks, multiple excitations, or active components are required.

articleTitle: Compact Eight-Port QMSIW Cavity Backed MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An 8-port modified-shielded quarter mode substrate integrated waveguide (MS-QMSIW) multiple-input-multiple–output (MIMO) antenna for WLAN applications is presented in this letter. The MIMO antenna comprises four MS-QMSIW resonators that are placed adjacent to each other, sharing the via side walls. Each MS-QMSIW resonator is inset fed orthogonally through a pair of microstrip feed lines. It utilizes the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</sub> mode of the QMSIW resonator for the radiations at 5.5 GHz. The designed MIMO antenna can be easily re-designed in a 4.6 GHz to 6.4 GHz frequency band by varying one of the design parameters without changing the overall size. The isolation between the antenna elements is better than 22 dB over the entire operating band. The antenna exhibits a gain of 5.75 dBi and a radiation efficiency of better than 85%.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Metasurface-Based Beam-Scanning Circularly Polarized Folded Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) and electronically reconfigurable folded reflector antenna (ERFRA), which has wide-angle beam scanning performance, is developed and demonstrated. The CP-ERFRA comprises a receiver-transmitter metasurface (RTMS), an electronically reconfigurable metasurface (ERMS), and a metallic patch acting as the feeding source. The RTMS completely reflects the x-polarized incident waves and transmits the y-polarized waves into CP waves, and the ERMS is formed by integrating two PIN diodes in each meta-atom. By controlling the on–off state of PIN diodes, the ERMS can achieve 1-bit phase encoding and linear polarization conversion. Due to these RTMS and ERMS properties, the ERFRA can generate CP radiation with beam-control ability. A 16 × 16 CP-ERFRA is fabricated and tested to verify the feasibility of the proposed design. The experimental results show that the beam scanning angle is up to ±50°, and the peak gain and aperture efficiency are 18.8 dBic and about 16.5%, respectively.

articleTitle: Realization of Flat-Topped Electromagnetic Orbital Angular Momentum Vortex Wave With a Square Array
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) vortex waves are a potential solution to the issue of scarce spectrum resources. However, most of the OAM waves generated by array antennas are narrow beams, which have uncontrollable beamwidths. To increase the angular coverage of OAM waves, this letter discusses the realization of vortex electromagnetic waves with flat-topped radiation patterns. By constructing a piecewise function of the target flat-topped radiation pattern and adopting the synthesis method of Bessel-Fourier expansion, the radiation patterns of the flat-topped EM vortex wave can be realized. Our results show that the synthesized flat-topped OAM wave can keep the directivity stable in a given wide-angle range. This may provide theoretical support for wide-angle vortex EM communication technology.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Broadband Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna Based on Tri-modal
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A low-profile broadband circularly polarized metasurface antenna with a single-layer substrate is proposed. The metasurface is composed of nonuniform truncated corner square patches arranged in two different arrangements. The central part of the metasurface is a 2 × 2 array, while the outer part is surrounded by an additional 16 unit cells. The antenna is analyzed using characteristic mode analysis, revealing that it can expand its impedance and axial ratio bandwidth by exciting three modes. At frequencies below 3.2 GHz, modes 1 and 3 are excited, with a characteristic angle phase difference of approximately 90° between them. However, above 3.2 GHz, modes 3 and 4 are activated, also exhibiting a characteristic angle phase difference of about 90°. The design is simplified, and manufacturing costs are reduced by placing the metasurface and the coplanar waveguide feed on opposite sides of the substrate. On this basis, a prototype antenna is fabricated and measured. The overall size of the antenna is 0.45λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>× 0.45λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>× 0.0067λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> represents the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency in free space). The measured results show a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 66.7% [(2.47 to 4.94) GHz], a 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 75% [(2.0 to 4.4) GHz], and a peak gain of 5.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Low-Profile and Wideband Surface-Wave Antenna of Conical Beam for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a low-profile and wideband conical-beam surface-wave antenna for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications. The compact antenna consists of a grounded dielectric conical frustum and a wideband feeding structure at its center. By using an inverted-cone feeding probe and a gear-shaped parasitic patch, cylindrical surface waves are excited to produce conical radiation patterns over an ultrawide frequency range. A prototype of the proposed antenna of only 6 mm thickness is designed, fabricated, and measured. The measured results demonstrate that the designed surface-wave antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 93.9% from 6.38 to 17.67 GHz with peak gains varying from 3.6 to 8.2 dBi and conical-beam radiation with low cross polarization. Due to its extremely low profile, wide bandwidth, and omnidirectional coverage, our proposed antenna can be potentially useful for communication and radar systems mounted on the surface of airplanes and UAVs.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Attenuation Model Using Gaussian Process in Sub-THz Terrestrial Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Atmospheric elements affect signal propagation and cause significant signal loss called atmospheric attenuation, especially in high-frequency range including sub-THz frequencies. Atmospheric attenuation mainly consists of gaseous, fog, and rain attenuation and the traditional approach considers them separately to develop good prediction models. However, the traditional models are not accurate and even unavailable for the high-frequency range, such as sub-THz frequencies. In this letter, we propose a new attenuation model to predict atmospheric attenuation for terrestrial line-of-sight propagation at high frequencies, such as sub-THz. The proposed model is based on Gaussian process regression (GPR). To train our model with a big measurement dataset, we use a scalable variant of GPR called blockbox matrix–matrix Gaussian process. We validate our model with a dataset obtained from a long-term measurement campaign at sub-THz frequencies. Our experiments show that our model significantly outperforms the existing model. We also show that our model provides reliable prediction intervals of atmospheric attenuation.

articleTitle: Fan-Shaped Multibeam Metasurface Lens Antenna for High Crossover Levels and Stable Radiation Gain
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A fan-shaped multibeam antenna based on a metasurface (MS) lens is first proposed and validated in this letter. It features stable radiation gain and high beam-crossover levels that are attractive in high-quality beam-scanning applications. A simple multiport pillbox antenna is employed as the source antenna, while an MS lens is placed above it with an air gap for beamforming. The proposed MS antenna targeting 5G millimeter-wave band has a −10 dB impedance bandwidth from 26.9 to 29.9 GHz. It can generate five beams with a scanning range of ±30°. Remarkably, the beam-crossover levels are higher than −1.9 dB at the central frequency. The gain variation for each beam is within 1 dB for a 12° coverage range and 3.5 dB for the whole ±30° angle coverage range. Compared with previous reports, the proposed MS antenna shows great advantages in terms of electric performance and physical properties.

articleTitle: A Shared-Aperture Linearly/Circularly-Polarized Filtering Antenna Array with Low Profile
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A dual-band [(2.6, 3.5) GHz] shared-aperture filtering antenna array with a 0.067λ0 profile is proposed. The antenna array working at the high band has right-handed circular polarization (RHCP), while the array working at the low band exhibits linear polarization (LP). For the high-band subarray, parasitic patches are introduced to obtain a wide effective operation band, and substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavities are utilized to excite a radiation null, leading to a sharp roll-off at the lower band edge. For the low-band LP antenna subarray, two U-shaped metal strips are used to improve the impendence bandwidth and produce a radiation null, resulting in a sharp roll-off at the upper band edge. As a result, the two subarrays can be placed closely within the same aperture, and a high isolation of over 30 dB between them can be achieved. The antenna is prototyped and tested, and the high subarray has an effective bandwidth of (3.27 to 3.66) GHz with |S11|≤−10 dB, AR≤3 dB, and a stable gain of 9.5dBi, and the low subarray has an −10 dB impedance bandwidth of (2.49 to 2.75) GHz with a gain of 10.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Four-Mode Switchable Frequency-Selective Surface Featuring Wide-Band and Angular Stability
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a switchable frequency-selective surface with wide-band and angle-stable characteristics, which could independently manipulate the TE and TM incidences through four modes. Distributed compensation capacitors are designed to solve the problems of unequal impedances and inconsistent responses under different polarizations caused by the asymmetric structure. It also helps improve the miniaturization and oblique-incident performances of this work. Additionally, the transmission responses and field distributions of each layer are studied to verify the proposed principle. The operating mechanism under different waves is also analyzed through two equivalent-circuit models. The results show that the design achieves stable transmission and shielding behaviors from 0° to 55° incidences. In the transmission state, a passband of 32.9% is realized with a minimum insertion loss of 0.15 dB, while the shielding performance can be observed from low frequencies to 10 GHz. Finally, a prototype is fabricated, and reasonable measurement results are obtained.

articleTitle: An Efficient FDA Beampattern Synthesis Method Based on SCO Technology
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Frequency diverse array (FDA) exhibits a phenomenon of distance-angle coupling, and existing decoupling methods suffer from drawbacks, such as high sidelobe levels and computational inefficiency. However, traditional joint optimization methods face challenges of computational inefficiency and convergence issues by jointly optimizing frequency deviation and element positions. This letter proposes a FDA decoupling method based on sequential convex optimization technology, which employs Taylor expansion techniques to approximate this high-dimensional nonconvex optimization problem as a series of convex optimization subproblems, enabling efficient solution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method not only further improves the performance of the FDA antenna but also exhibits higher computational efficiency compared to heuristic optimization algorithms.

articleTitle: Endfire Substrate Integrated Dielectric Resonator Antenna With Dual-Beam Radiation for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm-wave) endfire substrate integrated dielectric resonator antenna is proposed to provide dual-beam radiation. The dual-beam radiation is caused by the multilayer rectangular dielectric resonator (DR) with metallic walls on both sides and air vias at the center, which are used to generate modified TE13δ mode and adjust the distribution of E-fields, respectively. The metallic walls, air vias, DR and feeding line can all be implemented with a printed circuit board (PCB) process, which enhances the integration level of the endfire dielectric resonator antenna. The theoretical analysis of the dual-beam radiation is provided to guide the practical design. Compared with the state-of-the-art designs, the proposed antenna not only achieves dual-beam radiation in endfire dielectric resonator antenna but also exhibits the capability of substrate integration and high radiation efficiency. For demonstration, a dual-beam prototype is fabricated and measured. The proposed antenna shows dual-beam radiation with ±61° beam direction and more than 13 dB suppression at the endfire direction.

articleTitle: Alumina 3-D Printed Wide-Angle Partial Maxwell Fish-Eye Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a wide-angle partial Maxwell Fish-Eye (PMFE) lens antenna for W-band millimeter-wave communication, which is realized by alumina 3-D printing using lithography-based ceramic manufacturing. To achieve the targeted permittivity profile, in addition to structural measures, the solid-state porosity of alumina, and hence its material permittivity, is controlled by tuning the sintering temperature. The relative permittivity of bulk alumina was set at 5.13 with a sintering temperature of 1350 °C instead of being 9.2 with a sintering temperature of 1650 °C. The fabricated 3-D lens with a diameter of 33.7 mm achieves a peak realized gain of 25 dBi at a frequency of 109.5 GHz at the boresight, demonstrating a field-of-view of ±42° with a planar lens surface.

articleTitle: Stepped Waveform Time-Modulated Multibeam Array With Beam Suppression Functionality
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Time-modulated array (TMA) naturally generates a large number of sidebands to achieve multibeam radiation. Conventional multibeam TMAs using rectangular modulation signals lack design flexibility, and recent high-flexibility designs are mostly theoretical without experimental validation. To balance flexibility and feasibility, this letter proposes a stepped waveform multibeam TMA with beam suppression functionality. It uses in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) time modulators with digital attenuators and 0/π phase shifters to independently generate stepped waveforms in both in-phase and quadrature channels. These waveforms can fit various complex modulation signals, enabling the realization of diverse multibeam radiations and the suppression of specific beams. Experimental verification is conducted on the same TMA hardware system, achieving a 5-beam TMA and a 4-beam TMA by adjusting the time-modulated signals. The suppressed beams achieve a suppression level of up to −36 dB, making it effective for anti-interference.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Epsilon-Near-Zero (ENZ) Cavity Antenna Array for Wide-Angle Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a low-profile epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) cavity antenna array is proposed to achieve wide-angle beam scanning. The proposed array utilizes four slot-fed cavity antenna elements that operate with the ENZ mode, in which the electric field presents a unique sign-function-like distribution. By properly designing the width of the ENZ cavity, a wide 3 dB beamwidth is achieved in a low profile to increase the beam scanning angle of the array configuration. Furthermore, the narrow width of the antenna element also facilitates a decreased spacing between array elements, enabling the use of the appropriate spacing to increase the scanning angle. Different from the conventional wide-angle beam-scanning arrays with high profile, the proposed ENZ cavity antenna array achieves a remarkable beam scanning angle of ±72° (±73° in the measurement) while maintaining a low profile of only 0.03 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, exhibiting the potential applications in low-profile phased array systems.

articleTitle: D-Band Corrugated Horn Antenna Using Multi-Layer Structured-Glass Technology
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter demonstrates the use of structured-glass waveguide (SGW) technology in a stackable multilayer configuration in order to exhibit the versatile nature of structured-glass in high-frequency and high-performance applications. A novel multilayer corrugated elliptic horn antenna composed of nine wafer layers is designed for operation in the D-band frequency range and exhibits the use of a circular waveguide feed line. In this manner, the SGW antenna design is introduced to the literature for the first time and demonstrated with the highest operating frequency to date for structured-glass-based waveguide components. Detailed build profiles are provided with reference to the structured-glass fabrication method. Two of the proposed antenna components are fabricated in order to validate the gain measurement. The measured results are shown to achieve highly accurate S-parameter results and beam patterns throughout the selected frequency range.

articleTitle: Gain Bandwidth Enhancement and Sidelobe Level Stabilization of mm-Wave Lens Antennas Using AI-driven Optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in optimizing the phase distributions of a lens antenna to significantly enhance the gain bandwidth and stabilize the sidelobe levels (SLLs) at the millimeter-wave band. Through an AI-driven antenna design method (self-adaptive Bayesian neural network surrogate-model-assisted differential evolution for antenna optimization (SB-SADEA), specifically), this work obtains a phase distribution that provides a wide gain bandwidth and stable SLLs from 24 to 33 GHz. A lens antenna with 20 × 20 unit cells is implemented based on the phase distribution. Results show a 1 dB bandwidth of 28.2%, and the SLLs have also been lowered compared to the reference design. The optimized lens antenna shows a stable gain with a range of 20.13 to 22.16 dB from 24 to 33 GHz, in comparison to the reference design that has a gain range of 16.70 to 26.43 dB over the same frequency spectrum. The measured results align well with the simulated results, verifying the effectiveness of the AI-driven antenna design optimization technique in enhancing the performance of a lens antenna.

Author Keywords: self-adaptive Bayesian neural network surrogate model-assisted differential evolution for antenna optimization (SB-SADEA)

articleTitle: A Versatile Digital Antenna Array Transceiving System With Online Self-Calibration
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Digital antenna array-based transceiving platforms are critical for research and development in modern wireless systems, covering 5G communications and beyond fields, satellites, and many other fields. However, existing low-cost platforms, such as software-defined radios, have limited antenna numbers, lack continuous data collection capability and do not support online array calibration. To contribute to filling these gaps, this letter presents a versatile design of a digital antenna array transceiving system. An antenna calibration network is designed to support online self-calibration of all transceiving channels. Utilizing a small onboard storage and the memory of a host computer, a continuous data capturing scheme is developed. The system is implemented and applied in over-the-air experiments for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection, demonstrating the effectiveness of the developed design and its potential to enable fast development and validation of wireless system applications.

articleTitle: Three-Polarization-Reconfigurable Antenna Array Implemented by Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In order to implement circular polarization (CP) reconfigure, a semicircular ring antenna array has been designed by using liquid metal (LM). The array consists of eight CP antenna elements and a continuous-feeding network. A pair of slots are corroded on the radiation patch, and tubes are glued to the slots. The reconfigurable polarization was achieved by changing the current at the antenna surface after pushing the LM flowing to cover the slot with a microflow pump, then generating two degenerate modes. Therefore, a linear polarization and a right-/left-handed CP can be reconfigured. To verify this design, the antenna prototype has been fabricated; and the measurement results prove that the newly designed antenna array can archive three polarization forms, also presenting good work performance.

articleTitle: An Antenna Beamwidth Estimation Method Based on Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes an antenna beamwidth (BW) estimation method for user equipment (UE) test systems using a base station (BS) emulator in the millimeter-wave band. The proposed method takes advantage of the fact that the BS antenna footprint can be approximated as an ellipse and detects the half-power boundary in field measurements based on support vector machine. In addition, both elevation and azimuth BWs are derived from geometric analysis of the detected ellipse boundary. This approach enables the estimation of BWs without assuming an antenna pattern model as in the conventional method. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through ray-tracing simulations in an urban scenario. The numerical results show that the root-mean-square errors of both BWs estimated by the proposed method are less than 2.0<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula> for a receiver interval of <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\text{2.0}\,\text{m}}$</tex-math></inline-formula>.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Electromagnetic Performance Predictions of a Hypersonic Radome Based on Variable Thickness Gradient Dielectric Multilayer Walls
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: High temperatures in hypersonic conditions induce variations in the dielectric parameters of radome materials, leading to a decline in electromagnetic (EM) performance, such as boresight error (BSE) and transmission loss (TL). This letter introduces a model for variable-thickness gradient dielectric multilayer walls, developed based on the 2-D steady-state temperature field with consideration of thermal conductivity variation at high temperatures within a porous Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ceramic radome. The BSE and TL of the radome within the Mach 5–7 speed range were computed using the time-domain finite integral (FITD) method. The findings indicated that the EM performance degradation was most pronounced in the radome nose area, with the extent of deterioration escalating as speed increased, while changes in other regions were slight. The concept of asymmetry in insertion phase delay (IPD) was proposed to quantitatively describe the distribution characteristics of IPD, and its relationship with BSE is identified. The proposed model enables more accurate prediction of the EM performance of hypersonic radomes and provides guidance for correcting and optimizing their performance in operation.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Fixed-Frequency Beam-Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna For Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The rapid development of 5G millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) applications has put forward higher requirements for antennas, such as low cost. In this letter, a novel dual-polarized (DP) fixed-frequency beam-scanning leaky-wave antenna based on ridge gap waveguide (RGW) is proposed, operating in 5G mm-Wave band. The antenna is composed of a row of DP radiation elements fed by two rows of RGWs arranged side by side. The working state of each DP element is controlled by two independent slot-control structures. A 96-element antenna prototype is simulated, fabricated, and measured. DP radiation property (±45°) is achieved, with independent scanning for each polarization. A scanning angle larger than 95° and the peak realized gain of 14.3 dBi are achieved for each polarization. The port isolation for two polarizations is lower than −30 dB in most observation bands. The experimental results agree well with the simulated results. The antenna shows the advantage of low cost, which is of significance to the 5G mm-Wave applications.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Wideband Patch Antenna Using Even and Odd Modes for 5G Terminal Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a low-profile wideband microstrip patch antenna (MPA) based on even and odd modes and its four-antenna module on a 5G terminal back cover. Two pairs of even and odd resonance modes, i.e., TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2,0</sub>, anti-TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2,0</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,3/2</sub> and anti-TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,3/2</sub> modes, each with independent tuning capability, are excited and combined for the first time to cover a wide impedance bandwidth. The proposed antenna with a low profile of 1 mm (0.01λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>) shows the −6 dB impedance bandwidth spans from 3.4 GHz to 4.2 GHz (21.1%). Then, a four-element multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) antenna module is configured on the typical back cover of a mobile terminal in a sequentially rotated layout. To improve the isolation further, four neutralization lines are utilized between the adjacent elements. To validate the concept, the proposed MIMO antenna module was fabricated and tested. Over 21 dB isolation can be achieved across (3.4 to 4.3) GHz with an edge-to-edge distance of 3 mm. This MPA module provides a promising solution to design a low-profile planar antenna for terminal devices with a wide impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: Broadband Whip Omnidirectional Enhanced Gain Antenna Using Full-Metal 3D Printing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A broadband end-fed whip omnidirectional enhanced gain antenna using full-metal 3-D printing technology is proposed in this letter. The antenna consists of two parts: a radiation unit part and a feed matching part. The antenna array formed by interleaving the inner and outer metal strips between the antenna elements enhances the directivity of the antenna. The feed matching part of the conical impedance transformer broadens the antenna bandwidth. The designed antenna has been simulated and verified to have good performance. The entire antenna length is 1.93<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula>. Finally, the prototype is fabricated using 3-D metal printing technology and measured. The measurement impedance fractional bandwidth is 18<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula> (2.17 GHz to 2.6 GHz). The measurement peak realized gain is 5.99 dBi. The proposed design has the advantages of broadband and enhanced gain, and is a good choice for modern wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: High-Gain Dual-Circular-Polarized Filtering Lens Antenna for Low-Cost 60 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel design of a high-gain dual-circular-polarized (dual-CP) filtering antenna for the 60 GHz millimeter-wave application. We utilize a planar dual-linear-polarized (dual-LP) filtering antenna to illuminate a dielectric lens to realize such a design. The lens consists of a CP polarizer and an array of phase shifters. The CP polarizer plays a role in converting linear-polarized waves into circular-polarized waves. Accordingly, dual-CP radiation can be realized under the illumination of the ±45° dual-polarized antenna source. The phase shifters can provide phase compensations to collimate the divergent waves into parallel ones for high gain. Such a lens can be readily fabricated by using a three-dimensional printing technique. Experimental results show that the proposed dual-CP filtering lens antenna has excellent filtering response, high gain, easy integration, and low fabrication cost.

articleTitle: 2-D Multibeam Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Modified Luneburg Lens
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a multibeam leaky-wave antenna (LWA) based on a modified Luneburg lens (LL) beamforming network is proposed. The antenna performs a simple structure and low profile with 2-D beam scanning. First, the modified LL serves as a beamforming network since its variation range ratio of refractive index can be determined by the relative permittivity of the substrate. This can be simply achieved using a printed circuit board technique rather than the square root of two of conventional LL. Then, the relationship between the input port angle and the multibeam angle is analyzed using the geometric-optical method. Finally, a high-scanning-rate LWA array based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons is designed, and its open-stopband is effectively suppressed. A prototype is simulated and fabricated. The measured results show that the proposed antenna has a multibeam range of −42° to 40° in the E-plane and a beam scanning range of −53° to 44° in the H-plane within 8–10.5 GHz, which agrees well with the calculation and simulation.

articleTitle: Terahertz Array-Feed Reflector Antenna for Wide-Angle Retrodirective and Adaptive Tracking Communication System
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a retrodirective array-feed reflector antenna for terahertz adaptive tracking communication systems. The gain reaches 35.3 dB at 216 GHz when the antenna works in single-horn-feed mode with receiving, and the side lobe level is lower than −25 dB. And for the retrodirective mode with transmitting, it automatically forms a reflected wave pointing to the direction of the incident wave. At vertical incidence, the retrodirective gain reaches 41.2 dB, and the scanning coverage corresponding to a 3 dB gain drop reaches <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\pm$</tex-math></inline-formula>22.5°. Measured results show that the proposed antenna is well matched, with reflections below −14.5 dB from 172 to 260 GHz. This antenna is suitable for retrodirective and adaptive tracking systems and terahertz communication systems.

articleTitle: Improving Impedance Calculations for Cylindrical Conformal Holographic Antenna With a Small Radius
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In recent years, the holographic antenna (HA) composed of impedance unit cells fed by surface waves has been developed rapidly. However, the cylindrical conformal holographic antenna (CCHA) has been recently designed with planar unit cell impedance, which will result in beam deterioration and loss of gain and efficiency. Therefore, a way to calculate the impedance of curved unit cells is presented in this letter. Compared with the planar impedance calculation (PIC), the efficiency of the HA using the curved impedance calculation (CIC) is increased from 17.05% to 19.13% with the fixed deflection angle θ of 0° when the radius of the cylinder is 18 mm. An approximate calculation for the impedance of arbitrary cylindrical radius is proposed based on the PIC and CIC, which can achieve a more convenient calculation of impedance without significantly affecting performance. It has been shown that the efficiency of the HA using the approximate impedance calculation (AIC) is increased from 17.05% to 19.42% under the same conditions compared with the HA using the planar impedance calculation. The efficiency can also reach about 20% in the case of a small radius and angle less than 20°, which is close to the efficiency of planar HA. The measured radiation efficiency is 21.48% with a small radius. The low efficiency of the CCHA has been improved.

articleTitle: A Broadband and Wide-Angle Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter for Mobile Microwave Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a broadband and wide-angle linear-to-circular polarization converter (LCPC) based on a three-layer transmissive metasurface is proposed, to solve the problem of efficiency degradation caused by polarization mismatch in mobile microwave wireless power transmission. The simulated results show that our proposed model has an axial ratio of less than 3 dB in the 4.24–6.24 GHz band (38.17% bandwidth) with a maximum insertion loss of 1.66 dB for normal incidence in both yz and xz plane. In addition, 50° incidence angle stability can also be achieved. To verify the feasibility, a sample with a total dimension of 300 × 300 × 5.105 mm3 is fabricated. The measured results demonstrate that our LCPC combines the advantages of broad band, wide angle, low loss, and low profile. With this LCPC, the received power is verified to remain stable when the polarization angle of the receiving antenna changes.

articleTitle: A Novel Tri-band Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Using characteristic modal analysis (CMA), this letter introduces a novel tri-band microstrip metasurface (MTS) circularly polarized (CP) antenna with dual sense. The radiation part of the antenna consists of double “king” shaped curved rings and cut corner units, and the feed network consists of orthogonal feeding slots and a T-shaped power divider. In order to clarify the design process of the proposed antenna, CMA is first performed on the 3 × 2 MTS units by replacing the rectangular units with lower radiating curved rings and adjusting the units edges to mitigate the resonance mode reverse current and achieve the CP. Subsequently, CMA is carried out on MTS loaded with feeding slots to stimulate resonance modes. The results show that three pairs of orthogonal modes constituting the CP are formed by the MTS unit modes and the slot modes excited by the feeding slots at frequencies of 7.75 GHz, 8.8 GHz, and 9.8 GHz, respectively. Finally, to verify the performance of the antenna, the incorporation of a T-shaped power divider is simulated. The prototype experiments validate the principle and design methodology, and the measured results are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Circularly-Polarized Inverted Quad-Ridged Elliptical Waveguide Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a balanced-feed circularly polarized inverted quad-ridged elliptical waveguide horn antenna with a low-axial ratio (AR) and elliptical radiation pattern. A wideband single-mode operation in dual polarizations is achieved based on initial analysis of the modes and field patterns within the inverted ridged elliptical waveguide, which is essential for achieving a broadband low AR. Furthermore, a slotted ridge is proposed to elegantly adjust the phase relationship between the two polarizations over the entire operating frequency range in response to the nonlinear variation in propagation phase velocity with frequency caused by elliptical nonrotational symmetric structures. The fabricated antenna exhibits a 66.7% relative bandwidth from 4 GHz to 8 GHz with an AR < 2.6 dB, reflection coefficient < −17 dB, and isolation > 35 dB for dual circular polarizations.

articleTitle: A Concise Maehly Approximation Implementation for Perturbated-MoM to Predict RCS of Uncertain Geometrical Targets
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a concise Maehly approximation implementation for perturbated-method of moment (MoM) (CMA-PM) is proposed for predicting the radar cross section (RCS) of uncertain geometrical targets. Nonuniform rational B-spline surfaces are used to construct models with adjustable shapes. Initially, the surface currents are expanded with the Chebyshev series and substituted with a rational function Maehly approximation to enhance the accuracy. Subsequently, the moment-matching solution is employed to obtain the surface-induced current distribution of a target with arbitrary shape variations. Lastly, the mean and variance of the RCS are computed by using the perturbation technique. Numerical results indicate that, compared with the novel indeterminate asymptotic waveform evaluation and the perturbational-CFIE, the proposed CMA-PM method offers enhanced precision for a wider range of shape variations and reduces the consumption of computing resources. In comparison to the Monte Carlo method, the proposed CMA-PM method can significantly reduce the computational time.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Transmitarray Using Matched Dipole-Spiral Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a wideband receive-and-transmit element suitable for linear-to-circular polarization applications is proposed, utilizing a combined field-circuit and conjugate matching design approach. The receiver comprises a wideband, linearly polarized kite-shaped dipole, while the transmitter is a wideband, circularly polarized spiral antenna. The two elements' excitation probes are interconnected through a central via, allowing for continuous rotation of the spiral element for phase compensation. To test the proposed design, a 0.24 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> thick transmitarray with 635 elements was constructed, and its performance was assessed. The results indicated a peak gain of 29.3 dBi and peak aperture efficiency of 55.5% within the band. The 1 dB gain bandwidth ranged from 22 to 28.5 GHz, corresponding to a bandwidth of 25.7%.

articleTitle: Light-Weight Low-Cost Tightly Coupled Dipole Array Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A lightweight, low-cost, tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) antenna is presented for wireless power transfer. A simple low-cost H-plane scanning booster layer is first introduced to improve the scanning ability in H-plane. Therefore, a consistent E- and H-plane scanning performance is achieved for the designed unit cell. In addition, a new 1-to-4 differential feed network using power dividers and exponentially tapered baluns is designed and utilized to excite the unit cell. Finally, a 5 × 13 finite array antenna prototype was designed, fabricated, and measured for wide beam scanning performance verification. Both the measured and simulated results confirm that the fabricated array antenna can have a wide and consistent scanning range of ±50° in both E-plane and H-plane over 4.3:1 impedance bandwidth. In addition, low cross-polarization levels of less than −30.5 dB are achieved for the fabricated low top-to-ground profile (0.4 <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{{\lambda}}_{{h}}}$</tex-math></inline-formula>) TCDA antenna.

articleTitle: Closely Arranged Broadband Isolated Monopole Pair Array Antenna by Using U-Shaped Resonator
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A closely arranged broadband isolated monopole pair (MP) array antenna using a U-shaped resonator is presented. In the design, the MP element is closely arranged with a short distance of only 6 mm for a compact size. To achieve a broadband isolation in the MP element, a U-shaped resonator is introduced for improving both isolation and impedance performances. Different from the traditional decoupling method using connection lines, the introduced U-shaped resonator works as a shunt-resonated coupling neutralizer. It cannot only neutralize the original coupling in both lower and upper frequency bands for a broadband isolation but also improve the input impedance for a broad impedance bandwidth. Finally, a prototype of the four-pair MP array was fabricated and measured for performance demonstration. The detailed measured results prove that the developed array can have an overlapped bandwidth of 3.2–4.45 GHz (32.7%) for both impedance and isolation. In addition, the envelope correlation coefficient of less than 0.11 and high total efficiency of higher than 80% are achieved for wireless terminal applications.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain Stacked Patch Antenna Array on Standard PCB for D-Band 6G Communications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we propose a wideband high-gain array antenna approach for 6G communications in D-band (110–170 GHz) wholly using industry-standard printed circuit board (PCB), based on the aperture coupled stacked patch structure. Notably, to enhance array gain, bandwidth and meanwhile to meet the low-cost PCB standard, we propose an antenna structure on a six-layers PCB in which two metal layers are placed between the top and bottom patch layers functioned as null ground layers and via connection to form via fences for the suppression of surface waves between all antenna elements. To characterize the antenna, a wideband WR6 waveguide to microstrip transition is designed to interface with the microstrip line feeding. Simulated designs and measurements of the fabricated antennas and test structures are described and analyzed. Measurements well agree with the simulations, achieving excellent results with 35 GHz bandwidth ranging from 123 to 158 GHz, and a peak measured array gain of 17.5 dBi for 16 antenna elements. The design approach is therefore a low-cost solution to meet the expected requirements of 6G communications in terms of bandwidth, gain, scalability, and ease of integration to radio frequency integrated circuits.

articleTitle: A 220 GHz High-Gain Low-Cost Slot Array Antenna With Integrated Fabry–Perot Cavity
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a 220 GHz planar high-gain slot array (SA) antenna with an integrated Fabry–Perot cavity (FPC). The sophisticated SA is fabricated by low-cost printed-circuit-board (PCB) technology, and an FPC structure is used to improve the gain. In contrast to the conventional FPC that requires large air gaps between feed and partial reflective surface (PRS), the proposed PRS is integrated with SA on double sides of a single substrate, resulting in a more compact and stable architecture. By using PCB and integrated FPC technology, the gain of this antenna can be 1.2 dB higher than a pure metal SA with the same scale, while the cost is much lower, and the profile increases slightly. For verification, a 220 GHz prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured. The simulated peak aperture efficiency (AE) is 69%, the experiments show a peak gain of 30.1 dBi and a total efficiency (TE) of 38.3%. The 3 dB gain bandwidth is 3.2%. Compared with congener sub-THz planar antennas using low-cost fabrication methods, this antenna can remain a relatively high AE and TE under the high gain (more than 30 dBi) condition, which can be a good candidate for terahertz wireless applications.

articleTitle: Compact Filtering Antenna Design Combining Field and Circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A compact filtering antenna with high selectivity is proposed for wireless terminal devices. Based on the inverted-F antenna (IFA) structure, newly introduced electromagnetic couplings are elaborately utilized to produce new coupling topologies for filtering property. Therefore, two radiation nulls are realized at the lower and upper stopbands. Then, a net reactance circuit based on the equivalent circuit of IFA is designed to generate two additional radiation nulls to further improve the out-of-band suppression level. By combining the above field and circuit design techniques, a filtering antenna with four controllable radiation nulls is designed, while maintaining a compact size of 0.18λ0 × 0.05λ0 × 0.01λ0 (where λ0 represents the wavelength in free space at 2.35 GHz). The impedance bandwidth ranges from 2.2 GHz to 2.5 GHz. The efficiency in both stopbands covering 1.9 GHz to 2.1 GHz and 2.6 GHz to 2.8 GHz is below −17 dB. In addition, the design of filtering structures has less impact on the efficiency within the working band.

articleTitle: Dual-Circularly Polarized Single-Element Patch Antenna With Compact Multiport Feeding
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) S-band patch antenna that makes use of a multiport setup to improve its radiation efficiency and compactness is presented. The design highlights a single-element patch with eight-port feeding, by using compact slot meandering. To the best of the authors' knowledge, no earlier literature discloses a similar single-element patch with eight feeding points made compact by slot meandering while demonstrating comparable performances, bandwidth, agility, and polarization purity. In addition, our design utilizes eight 50-<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\Omega$</tex-math></inline-formula> microstrip ports to set and excite the orthogonal polarization states. The miniaturized feeding arrangement, directly under the patch, enables the antenna to produce both left-handed and right-handed CP (as well as other polarization states), making the design suitable for full-duplex and diversity scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Patch Antenna Covering Four Bands with Pattern Diversity Property
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A single-layer miniaturized patch antenna with four covering bands and pattern diversity properties is presented. The pattern diversity derives from the superposition of equivalent multipoles. The driven circular patch could provide diverse magnetic current sources and meanwhile, the tightly coupled, parasitic monopole pair could provide two extra vertical electric current sources. Two broadside patterns are superposed by a pair of anti-phase vertical electric current sources and a pair of in-phase magnetic current sources from the TM11 mode of the circular patch with a 90° delay/advance. A dual beam along the y-axis is achieved by the superposition of a pair of in-phase vertical electric current sources and a pair of anti-phase magnetic currents from the circular patch with a 90° delay. Further, an x-axis-oriented dual beam takes advantage of a pair of in-phase vertical electric current sources and two pairs of anti-phase magnetic current sources from the TM21 mode of the circular patch with a 90° delay. Its multi-band and pattern diversity properties make it meet the requirements of vehicular communication applications.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Dielectric Reflectarray Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A highly proficient and compact 3-D-printed dielectric reflectarray (DR) antenna is engineered, fabricated, and tested to ensure wideband functionality for millimeter-wave satellite communication (SATCOM). Initially, a dielectric metamaterial unit cell (UC) having a periodicity of 0.28λ0 (here, λ0 is the free-space wavelength at 28 GHz) is proposed. Next, a DR structure is meticulously designed by arranging eight different variants of the proposed UC in an 18 × 18 array according to the obtained 3 b quantized phase profile, resulting in an overall aperture area of 25.4${\lambda }_0^2$. The proposed DR is primarily analyzed for its performance using radiation pattern analysis based on array theory followed by full-wave simulation. The entire DR antenna setup consists of a 3-D-printed horn antenna acting as a primary feed source, placed at a separation of 47 mm from DR along the +z-direction supported by a 3-D-printed structural framework. The DR antenna is additively manufactured, and its performance evaluation is done in an anechoic chamber revealing a measured half-power bandwidth of 43% with a peak gain of 23.8 dBi at 28 GHz, showcasing a notable gain enhancement of 9.7 dB compared to prior designs, translating to a remarkable maximum aperture efficiency of 75%.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Diplexer-Antenna Array with Low Sidelobe Level Based on Gap Waveguide at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a 1 × 8-element dual circularly polarized (CP) diplexer-antenna array with a low-sidelobe level is proposed at Ka-band for satellite communication links. Integrated diplexer to the antenna is achieved by embedding filter-splitters consisting of a cascade of resonators in the feeding network. The dual CP is obtained by asymmetric feeding on both sides of the slot element. The sidelobe level is suppressed by weighting the current amplitude of the antenna element by the Chebyshev array. Finally, the proposed dual CP diplexer-antenna array prototype is fabricated. The measured results show that the realized gains are higher than 17.3 dBic and 17.9 dBic in both of the two operating passbands (34 GHz to 35 GHz and 36 GHz to 37 GHz), and the efficiency is greater than 60%. The sidelobe level on the yz-plane is lower than −19.4 dB for the dual CP radiation. Moreover, the isolation between the two ports is up to 60 dB, achieving extremely low interference between dual channels.

articleTitle: A Wideband Substrate Integrated Filtering Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a wideband substrate integrated dielectric resonator (SIDR) antenna with filtering response for millimeter-wave (mm wave) applications is proposed. The antenna contains a dual-mode SIDR, which is fed by a slot-coupled double-T-shaped microstrip feeding structure. The stacked substrates with the peripheral air vias and a metallic via cavity are the main body of the SIDR, which ensure dual-mode operation with the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">111</sub> mode and the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</sub> mode. The pair of strips, the small patches with shorting pins and the two center air vias are the accessory parts of the SIDR, which play roles of converting the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</sub> mode into the perturbed-TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">131</sub> mode, providing radiation nulls, and improving the out-of-band suppression level. The double-T-shaped feeding structure has two pairs of stubs with different lengths, providing a radiation null and a reflection zero, improving the impedance matching of the slot resonant mode and enhancing the suppression level at the upper stopband. For demonstration, a prototype of 1 × 4 array is designed and measured. The prototype operating at 24 GHz has a 10 dB impedance matching bandwidth of 34% (19.8–27.9 GHz), a peak gain of 13.1 dBi, and an out-of-band suppression level of about 21 dB.

articleTitle: A Duplexing Filtering Antenna With Small Frequency Ratio and High Isolation Using Hanging Resonators
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A duplexing filtering antenna based on hanging resonators is presented. The antenna is mainly composed of seven cavities. A square cavity operating in TE101 and TE011 modes is located at the top, and a pair of metal posts is introduced at the diagonal line to control the coupling between the two modes. Then, by utilizing slots along the x-axis, only the TE101 mode radiates and is coupled to both the low- and high-frequency channels. Therefore, the TE011 mode is hanging from the TE101 mode, and a transmission zero can be generated between the two channels. Each of the two channels consists of three cavities placed under the square cavity. The three cavities are sequentially coupled through inductive irises, and the middle cavity is excited by a coaxial input port. The bottom cavity acts as a hanging resonator and produces a transmission zero when it resonates. To verify the design, a prototype is manufactured and tested, whose measured results show a good agreement with the simulated ones. Three transmission zeros can be observed, and the interport isolation is above 39.4 dB and 34.5 dB in the low- and high-frequency bands, respectively.

articleTitle: High-Transmission Quasi-Optical Faraday Rotators Based on Multi-layer Matching
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Due to the inherent nonreciprocity of magnetic materials, Faraday rotators constructed based on these materials are the optimal passive isolation solution for compact range systems. In this letter, we propose a theoretical method of multisection matching transformation to analyze the reflection characteristics of anisotropic magnetic ferrite coated with multilayer isotropic dielectric layers. Utilizing this approach, a bilayer-matching transmission-type broadband quasi-optical Faraday rotator (QOFR) is designed to achieve reflection coefficient below 20<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\text{ dB}$</tex-math></inline-formula> in the 86 GHz to 141 GHz range. Compared to quarter-wave matching designs, it improves the operational bandwidth by 30% and stabilizes the ferrite rotation angle at 45° ± 0.7°. A transceiver isolation system for the compact range is constructed based on this QOFR. Its performance is measured on a quasi-optical platform. Additional theoretical analysis aims to identify factors that influence measured performance, especially the impact of gaps in multilayer dielectric materials. The CST and HFSS simulation results align with measurements and verify the accuracy of the proposed theoretical approach and design.

articleTitle: A Miniaturised Triple-band MIMO Antenna with Dual-band Circular Polarisation for Leadless Pacemaker
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents the development of a triple-band multiple-input–multiple-output implantable antenna with dual-band circular polarization (CP) performance for leadless pacemakers. The proposed antenna operates across the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical band (2.4 GHz to 2.48 GHz), Midfield band (1.5 GHz to 1.75 GHz), and Wireless Medical Telemetry Service band (608 MHz to 614 MHz), respectively. In addition, the designed antenna features a symmetrical and compact structure that is constructed within a leadless pacemaker and optimized in a realistic human heart phantom. Simulation results demonstrate that the designed antenna achieves impedance bandwidths of 13.33%, 12.5%, and 33.33%, with peak realized gains of –28.9 dBi, –38.4 dBi, and –41.7 dBi at 2.45 GHz, 1.65 GHz, and 610 MHz, respectively. Moreover, the antenna exhibits left-handed CP functionality at 2.45 GHz and 1.65 GHz. Finally, the proposed antenna is fabricated and measured in the minced pork, which verifies the simulated results.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Channel Frequency-, Space- and Object- Consistency At the W-Band
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Subterahertz (sub-THz) frequencies provide huge untapped bandwidth for high data rates in wireless communications and high-precision sensing applications. Understanding radio channel characteristics at sub-THz frequency bands is important to identify potential applications. This letter investigated the frequency dependence, spatial consistency, and impact of blockage at the W-band. Employing the vector-network-analyzer-based virtual antenna array channel sounder, several wideband measurements covering three frequency bands, eight spatial locations, with or without the blockage at the W-band were performed. The experimental analysis demonstrated that channel characteristics have good frequency consistency and a strong correlation with the spatial environment. The above research is of great significance for achieving fast beam alignment and channel prediction in different spatial locations.

articleTitle: Differential and Symmetrical Decoupling Network for Differentially Fed Antennas
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes the differential and symmetrical decoupling network (DSDN), a novel method specifically designed to decouple differentially fed antennas (DFAs) while preserving their structural symmetry. DFAs offer several advantages over single-fed antennas (SFAs) due to their symmetrical design, but the presence of multiple antenna ports and coupling paths poses challenges for decoupling. Existing methods for SFAs disrupt the structural symmetry of DFAs. The DSDN significantly enhances the isolation between DFAs, and its effectiveness is validated through theoretical derivations, simulations, and experimental measurements on a 1 × 2 DFA array and a 1 × 4 DFA array. The results demonstrate isolation improvements of 53 and 40 dB at the center frequency for the 1 × 2 and the 1 × 4 DFA array, respectively, compared with the coupled array. The DSDN offers a promising solution for decoupling DFAs, allowing for significantly improved performance while maintaining structural symmetry.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Heterogeneous Stacked Patch Antenna with Stable Radiation Performance and High Efficiency
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a ±45° dual-polarized heterogeneous stacked patch antenna with stable radiation performance and high efficiency is presented for the 5G massive multiple-input–multiple-output (M-MIMO) base station. It comprises a driven metallic patch (MP) and a parasitic dielectric patch (DP), which induce low- and high-frequency resonant modes, respectively. The excitation of the top DP is achieved by the bottom MP through four supporting dielectric blocks between them, which allow for surface-mounted technology installation of the DP. Furthermore, the utilization of DP for generating high-frequency mode enables the heterogeneous antenna to have an efficiency of >90% in a bandwidth (|S11| < −15 dB) of 14.1% (3.3 GHz to 3.8 GHz). The off-center configuration of the four dielectric blocks increases the equivalent dielectric constant of the sidewall of the heterogeneous radiator, resulting in stable radiation patterns. The variations of realized gain and half-power beamwidth are below 0.3 dBi and 5°, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Polarized FSS With Wide Angular Stability and High Selectivity
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a wide angle and high selective bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) based on meandering square slot resonators. The proposed FSS mainly consists of five square annular slots deployed in a three-layer structure. To elucidate the operating principle, an equivalent circuit model is constructed and analyzed. The results indicate the generation of a passband with three transmission poles (TPs) and two independently controllable transmission zeros (TZs). By applying this principle, three types of S-parameters with different frequency locations of TZs are achieved. One prototype was fabricated and measured, demonstrating that the proposed structure possesses attractive advantages such as wide passband, controllable TZs, polarization insensitivity, high selectivity, and stable performance at a maximum oblique incidence angle of 60°.

articleTitle: A Dual Component Electromagnetic Probe for Efficient Near-Field Measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a dual-component vertical electric field Ez and vertical magnetic field Hz probe is proposed for efficient near-field measurement, which can be divided into the coupling section and the receiving section. The coupling section consists of magnetic coupling loops inducing the magnetic field Hz and electric coupling monopoles inducing the electric field Ez. The receiving section transmits the induced signals to a receiving device with good impedance matching. The equivalent circuit model is built to show that the common mode voltage and the differential mode can be used to measure Ez and Hz, respectively. The proposed probe is designed and fabricated under a printed circuit board (PCB) and calibrated by the microstrip line and the slotline for Ez and Hz, respectively. The measured results show the proposed probe has a spatial resolution of 0.7 mm for Ez and 1.2 mm for Hz at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Gain Anomaly Mitigation in Coaxial-Fed Log- Periodic Dipole Array Using Wideband Φ-Shaped Balun
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) is always plagued by the gain anomaly together with pattern deflection caused by unbalanced coaxial feeding—an issue without a universal solution. In this letter, a novel Φ-shaped balun is proposed to address the issue. Both the current and electric field have provided the physical mechanism of the Φ-shaped balun in the elimination of the gain anomaly. The Φ-shaped balun not only performs the unbalanced to balanced conversion but also performs a wideband impedance transformation. Moreover, owing to the compact planar configuration, the proposed Φ-shaped balun is easy to integrate into the RF circuit without compromising the antenna performance. Finally, the proposed prototype is fabricated and measured for demonstration. The measured results demonstrate that Φ-shaped balun eliminates the unbalanced current caused by the coaxial feeding, thus the LPDA exhibits stable radiation performance with an average gain of 7 dBi, without pattern deflection and gain anomaly within the operating frequency range of 0.9–2 GHz.

articleTitle: Single-Substrate Transmissive Antenna Radiating Arbitrary Symmetric Multibeams Based on Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, an approach to designing the symmetric multibeam metasurface (MS) based on 1-bit coding sequences is put forward and its effectiveness is verified. Also, a single-substrate element with the transmissive coefficient of −0.63 dB is designed to reduce the profile and improve the gain. Moreover, the amplitude and the phase of the element could be regulated independently so that the element could be employed to suppress the sidelobe level (SLL). Finally, based on the proposed approach and the element, a low SLL transmissive dual-beam antenna employing a single-substrate coding MSs is constructed. The measured result shows that, at 15 GHz, the antenna has a gain of 15.9 dBi and SLL of −16.9 dB. The −1.5 dB gain bandwidth of the antenna is from 14.78 to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS Reduction Metasurface Based on Printing Resistive Graphene Ink
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel approach to constructing 1-bit coding unit cells for metasurface design and utilizes a genetic algorithm to effectively reduce the radar cross section (RCS) of the antenna over a wide frequency range. Unlike previous methods, this approach allows for manipulation of the coding state of unit cells by modifying the sheet impedance of resistive graphene rather than altering conventional metallic structures. The 1-bit coding units “0” and “1” can be achieved by utilizing graphene Rs values of 10 and 1000 Ω/sq, respectively, resulting in a reflection response with a phase difference of π and relatively large amplitude. The measurement results were compared with full-wave simulation ones to benchmark the performance of the proposed antenna. The antenna achieves more than 10 dB RCS reduction band from 12.5 to 27.7 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 75.6%. The proposed design exhibits promising potential applications in stealth technology for intricate entities.

articleTitle: Compact Four-Port MIMO Antenna Module With Decoupling Components for 5G Terminal Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This study investigated the decoupling mechanism of capacitors in multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) antenna designs based on characteristic mode analysis (CMA). First, a two-port single-loop antenna, where shunt capacitor elements were used to obtain high port-to-port isolation properties, was analyzed. CMA revealed that the decoupling capacitors’ mechanism lies in the modal superposition of the original radiation mode (Mode-2) and the manipulated high-order mode (Mode-3) with anti-phase current distributions. Accordingly, a compact four-port MIMO antenna module based on decoupling components (inductors and capacitors) was designed as the first of its kind. Both simulations and measurements were conducted to verify the feasibility of the proposed MIMO antenna module.

articleTitle: A Compact Multifrequency Broadband Dual-Antenna System With Mutual Coupling Reduction for Wi-Fi 6E Application
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a compact multifrequency broadband dual-antenna system with mutual coupling reduction for Wi-Fi 6E application is proposed. The dual-antenna system consists of two identical inverted-F antennas (IFAs), and the minimum distance of two antennas is only 2 mm, yet the antenna system occupied a small size of 6.5 × 41 mm2 (about 0.05λmin × 0.32λmin, λmin is the wavelength at the lowest frequency). A decoupling inductor is induced between two open ends of two antennas for lower band decoupling, while a modified decoupling branch and a modified neutralization line are introduced between two antennas for upper wide band decoupling. After adopting the three decoupling techniques, the dual-antenna system obtains remarkable isolation with |S21| > 22 dB in all desired bands of WLAN 2.4 GHz/5 GHz (2.4–2.484 GHz, 5.15–5.35 GHz, 5.725–5.825 GHz) and Wi-Fi 6E (5.925–7.125 GHz). These presented decoupling techniques are compact and low-cost and can be used for those designs of multifrequency broadband dual-antenna systems without adding extra size.

articleTitle: 360°-Beam-Steering Low-Sidelobe Time Reversal Microwave Power Transfer by Superposition of Multiple Weighted Radiation Modes
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a 360°-beam-steering low-sidelobe time reversal microwave power transfer (TR-MPT) method. The beam steering is implemented by only one circular patch antenna fabricated with multiple feeding ports. The multiple feeding ports are designed to stimulate different radiation modes and their combinations to steer the beam within 360° in the azimuth plane. To depress the sidelobe levels and enhance the beam gain, a disc-top-loaded monopole antenna is added at the center of the patch antenna, which is used to excite an additional mode out of phase with the maximal sidelobe but in phase with the main lobe. Finally, time reversal (TR) is adopted for optimally weighting the stimulated modes and focusing the power beam adaptively to the desired receiver. A prototype of the TR-MPT system based on the proposed method is established. The experiments demonstrate that the new method can not only adaptively focus the power at the receiver placed at any azimuth angle within 360°, but also achieve a low sidelobe level of smaller than −8.57 dB under a 0.7-wavelength aperture. Additionally, the power transferred to the receiver at different angles has a small fluctuation of less than 0.7 dB.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Trimmed MLFMA Using the PO Method for Large-Scale Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The physical optics (PO) method is used to improve the convergence and the computational efficiency of the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA), which involves distributing the global linear system into two algorithmic subsystems and trimming the octree structure. The PO subsystem generates most of the contribution to the global system, resulting in a smaller but not negligible contribution from the MLFMA subsystem. The octree structure in the MLFMA subsystem is trimmed by evaluating the contribution of the PO subsystem to the global system, which can reduce the matrix–vector product computation and improve the convergence of the MLFMA subsystem. The results show a significant acceleration effect for large-scale electromagnetic scattering simulations, and the proposed method achieves higher accuracy than the high-frequency asymptotic method.

articleTitle: Wideband Multiport Antenna Design by Sub-Array Aperture Sharing Offering Dual-Circularly Polarized Beamforming for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This work proposes a low-cost, low-profile, and wideband antenna with the capability of dual-circularly polarized (DCP) radiation. The design concept utilizes a common and shared subarray aperture for both circularly polarized (CP) states, achieving competitive performances. The basic structure comprises five patch elements and the first state, CP1, is achieved by a central patch, while the second state, CP2, is made possible by the placement of four surrounding patches. Sequential rotation is employed and this realizes polarization purity in terms of low axial ratios (ARs) and cross-polarization levels. In addition, the design lends itself to larger scale arrays as reported in this letter. The measured results for the fabricated prototype are in agreement with the simulations, demonstrating an impressive impedance bandwidth (BW) of about 22.8% for both states (2.23 GHz to 2.80 GHz) and a 3 dB AR-BW of 24.6% (2.21 GHz to 2.83 GHz). In addition, the antenna is simple and can be a suitable candidate for satellite systems and wireless communications, and generally where DCP radiation is required. As further outlined in the letter, the proposed multiport design can also be useful for DCP wireless power transfer systems, which operate on array principles.

articleTitle: 3-D-Printed CRLH Metamaterial-Enabled Electrically Small Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a 3-D-printed composite right/left-handed (CRLH) metamaterial-enabled electrically small antenna (ESA) in the 300 MHz band. A 3-D conical helix strip is loaded by surrounding an electrical small monopole antenna, with a length of 0.02<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\lambda _{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula> (free space wavelength), which is vertically placed over a finite ground plane. The proposed ESA is based on the 3-D realization of an open-ended CRLH resonator, of which the electrical size is <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ka$</tex-math></inline-formula> = 0.11. An equivalent circuit model is provided with corresponding circuit parameters to derive the frequency response of the proposed 3-D-CRLH ESA. A prototype is fabricated using a widely available 3-D print technology, fused filament fabrication, combined with copper electro- and electroless plating. Experimental verification of the antenna demonstrates a monopole-like radiation pattern with a peak measured gain of −5 dBi, which is suitable to be integrated into compact wireless systems.
