articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Beam-Scanning Reflectarray With Switchable Polarization Using Independently Controlled Dual-Linearly Polarized Units
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a pattern- and polarization-reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (RRA). Using 1-bit independently controlled dual-linearly polarized (DLP) units, the radiation beam of the RRA can be scanned with switchable polarization. The designed unit is composed of a crossed dipole, a metallic centered patch, four PIN diodes and biasing networks. By controlling the working states of the PIN diodes, the unit possesses independently 180° reflection phase shift in either of the two linear polarizations (LPs). A novel polarization manipulation method is introduced, and the 1b DLP unit can be transformed into a 2b unit with agile polarization. Based on the DLP unit, the proposed RRA can realize polarization reconfigurable among ±45° LPs, left-hand circular polarization and right-hand circular polarization by only changing the biasing voltages applied on the RRA. A prototype including 256 units is analyzed, fabricated, and measured. The 2-D beam-scanning ability is verified for dual-linear polarization and reconfigurable polarization. Good performance, including high gain and good polarization purity, can be observed. The proposed RRA features a wide beam scanning range and agile polarization, which makes it a good candidate for the wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Compact Slow-Wave Half-Mode SIW Periodic Leaky-Wave Antenna with Continuous Beam Scanning and High Gain
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A compact periodic leaky-wave antenna (PLWA) with continuous beam scanning characteristics and high gain is proposed based on a slow-wave half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SW-HMSIW). The SW-HMSIW is designed on the basis of normal HMSIW by loading SW structures, consisting of metalized blind vias and patches, decelerating the phase velocity of an electromagnetic wave traveling in SIW, reducing the guided wavelength by 50%. Thus, the distance between the adjacent radiating slots in HMSIW PLWA is decreased by half, allowing twice as many radiating slots in SW-HMSIW PLWA with the same length. Then, the gain of such PLWA can be significantly increased. Besides, the loaded patches of SW structure under the radiating slots are extended to improve the impedance match of the radiating units, contributing to the open-stopband suppression. In consequence, the radiation beam can scan from backward to forward direction continuously. A prototype of the proposed SW-HMSIW PLWA is manufactured and measured. The total scanning angle of the proposed SW-HMSIW PLWA reaches 62.3° during the operating frequency range of (13.7 to 15.7) GHz with maximum gain of 11 dBi. The measured results agree well with the simulations.

articleTitle: Compact 2-D Frequency-Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna Array With Cyclically Progressive Phase-Shifting Feeding Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel method to realize a 2-D frequency-scanning leaky-wave antenna (LWA) array with a compact architecture feature is proposed in this paper. As the operating frequency is swept, beam-scanning in the E-plane depends on the intrinsic phase shift along the longitudinal direction of the LWA, while the progressively manipulated phase shift of the embedded feeding network along the cross-sectional direction results in the scanning behavior in the other coupled scan dimension (H-plane). To broaden beam-scanning range, a maximum beam pointing in the broadside direction is designed. Based on the above method, a 2-D frequency-scanning LWA array is designed, fabricated and measured; the results show that the impedance bandwidth achieves 29.9%, and the maximum gain is 19 dBi. Besides, the scanning beam is capable of covering an area of 60° × 180° (θ×φ) by changing frequency from 14 to 16.8 GHz.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Independent Multifunctional Active Frequency Selective Surface With Compound Modes of Absorption, Transmission, and Reflection
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A polarization-independent multifunctional active frequency selective surface (MAFSS), which possesses electromagnetic switching and polarization selection functions, is proposed in this letter. Three compound modes of absorption, transmission, and reflection are attained in the same working band. The proposed MAFSS consists of a switchable transmission/lossy layer, an air spacer, and a switchable transmission/reflection layer. Each reconfigurable functional layer contains PIN diodes that can be controlled separately for different polarizations. Thus, the proposed design can achieve nine different working states in a single structure with dual-polarized properties. The equivalent circuit approach is employed to explain the physical principles of the proposed design. Finally, a prototype is fabricated for validation and the measured results show a good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: A Pattern Shaping Method for Focused Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, the extended method of maximum power transmission efficiency (EMMPTE) is applied to the design of the antenna array to generate desired field patterns in the target region. By introducing different weighted constraints, the EMMPTE ensures the high electric field intensity in the target region while its distribution pattern can be flexibly controlled. Once the weighted matrix is determined, a focused electric field pattern with the desired shape can be generated by the antenna array with the optimized distribution of excitations obtained from solving the weighted constrained problem. To verify the validity of the proposed method, a 6 × 6 microstrip antenna array operating at 2.45 GHz is designed and fabricated to produce four different focused near-field patterns—a square, a circle, a triangle and a heart-shaped pattern. Measurement results show a good agreement with simulations.

Author Keywords: method of maximum power transmission efficiency

articleTitle: A High-Isolation SIW Self-Octaplexing Antenna With Independent Frequency Tuning Capability
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents an eighth mode substrate integrated waveguide (EMSIW)-based eight-channel self-multiplexing antenna for sub-6 GHz wireless applications for the first time. Asymmetric slots are etched on the EMSIW cavities to make the antenna radiate at eight different frequencies. The antenna has independent frequency tuning capability, high isolation (30–46 dB), acceptable peak realized gains (4.07–5.11 dBi), and a good front-to-back radiation ratio (20 dB).

articleTitle: Leakage-Free Leapfrog ADI-FDTD Method for Lossy Media
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The leapfrog alternating direction implicit finite-difference time-domain (ADI-FDTD) method, as an effective implementation of ADI-FDTD, has garnered widespread attention and extension. However, it has been found that the commonly used leapfrog ADI-FDTD method for lossy media exhibits field leakage whereby nonzero electromagnetic fields could leak through structures that should be nonpenetrable, such as perfect electrical conductor structures. This numerical flaw limits the broader application of the leapfrog ADI-FDTD method. To address this issue, this article introduces a leapfrog ADI-FDTD method for lossy media free from field leakage. The method is derived from the unified ADI-FDTD formulation employing the fundamental scheme with matrix-operator-free right-hand sides. Numerical results demonstrate that the method is not only immune to field leakage issue but also yielding higher accuracy when modeling lossy media. Furthermore, due to the utilization of the fundamental scheme, it requires less computational operations compared with the conventional leapfrog ADI-FDTD method for lossy media.

articleTitle: Homogeneous Microwave Near-Field Power Focusing Using Conjugate Electric Field Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces a novel near-field microwave power focusing approach termed the conjugate electric field (CEF) method for any arbitrary focusing point within the studied area. Using a cylindrical circumferential array with electric line source elements in a homogeneous medium with zero magnetic loss, the CEF method obtains excitation signals based on the complex conjugate of the electric field from a virtual source at the desired focusing point. Assigning weights determines array element participation, enabling focus with fewer elements. Theoretical findings are validated through full-wave simulations and obtained excitation signals are applied to the same array with half-wave dipole antenna elements. Two examples of this array in the fatty tissue medium demonstrate consistent and identical focusing behavior aligning with theoretical results. Finally, comparing the time to obtain excitation signals through theoretical analysis with the time required by the full-wave method assesses the efficiency and speed of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Reflective Metasurface for OAM and Polarization Multiplexing Communication in the W-Band
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a reflective metasurface for orbital angular momentum (OAM) and polarization multiplexing communication is proposed in the W-band. To realize OAM and polarization multiplexing communication, not only the design principle of the metasurface is studied, but also the reflective unit capable of being modulated in two polarizations and working in broad bandwidth is designed. Experimental results show that it can generate the multiplexed OAM beams in two polarizations with high mode purities. After measuring the great isolation performance provided by different OAM modes and polarizations, the four generated beams are employed as multiplexing channels to transmit the communication signals with quadrature phase shift keying format, and the data rate reaches 64 Gb/s at last. With the assistance of metasurface, OAM multiplexing technology has shown great potential in large-capacity wireless communication.

articleTitle: Experimental Over-the-Air Diagnosis of 1-Bit RIS Based on Complex Signal Measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), is regarded as a promising technology for enhancing wireless system performance. The RIS design typically comprises a substantial number of cost-effective RIS elements. RIS diagnosis, which aims at identifying faulty RIS elements, is essential to ensure the RIS functions as intended. In this letter, a low-cost, robust, fast, yet highly effective over-the-air diagnosis method based on complex signal measurements is proposed to detect the faulty phase shifters in passive 1-bit RISs. This method only requires a phase inversion operation (i.e., 0<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^\circ$</tex-math></inline-formula> and 180<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^\circ$</tex-math></inline-formula> phase states) for each RIS element. The algorithm is experimentally validated using a commercial RIS operating at 3.5 GHz in a mid-field anechoic measurement setup, (i.e., with a measurement distance much smaller than the Fraunhofer far-field distance of the RIS) demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness in practical setups.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Wideband Self-Oscillating Active Integrated Antenna with Power Enhancement
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a compact and wideband self-oscillating active integrated antenna (AIA) with power enhancement. It consists of a dc-charged wideband antenna with large equivalent capacitance and a pulse-triggered network controlling its working states. In the design, a capacitively coupled region is created in the antenna, which not only improves the frequency bandwidth but also enhances the energy storage capacity. Consequently, the proposed design enables greater energy storage within the antenna in the charging state, thereby significantly increasing the radiated power in the radiation state. Measured results show that the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of the proposed AIA is approximately 8 dB greater than the EIRP of the self-oscillating AIA employing a conventional dipole antenna, while the system size is only 0.1λ<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$ \,\times\, $</tex-math></inline-formula> 0.1λ at the frequency that corresponds to the maximum output power.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Tunable Dielectric Resonator Antenna With Rotatable Anisotropic Metasurface
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces a frequency-tunable dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) with a top-loaded rotatable anisotropic metasurface. The metasurface at different angles can be equivalent to materials with different permittivity. As a result, the frequency of the DRA operating at TMδ11 mode can be continuously adjusted. The working mechanism of the proposed tunable DRA is given in detail. Since both the mechanical tuning scheme and DR are adopted, the proposed design shows high efficiency (low loss) and small size. For demonstration, a differential-feeding prototype is fabricated and measured. The center frequency can be tuned from 6.64 to 6.96 GHz as the metasurface is rotated by 90°. Within it, the radiation pattern is stable, and the radiation efficiency is more than 76%.

articleTitle: A Design Methodology of Broadband Millimeter-Wave Conical Radiating Antenna Based on Ring-Shaped Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A design methodology based on ring-shaped microstrip antenna for wideband conical radiating antenna is presented in this letter. This design approach allows for flexible antenna beam pointing while maintaining broadband characteristics. The enhanced bandwidth is based on dual-mode resonance. One resonance mode is evolved from TE<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$_{{\text{1}}}$</tex-math></inline-formula> mode of the microstrip line, the other one is achieved by disrupting the quasi-TEM mode with asymmetric excitation. The ring-shaped microstrip lines of different sizes can be excited to work at the same required frequency band by adjusting the number of excitation points, to realize the adjustment of the antenna radiation beam pointing. In this letter, three different antennas are analyzed in detail, and a case with seven feeding points is tested and verified. The measured results show that a bandwidth of 13.4% (32.1–36.7 GHz) is achieved on a single-layer substrate with a conical radiation gain greater than 10 dBi.

articleTitle: Optimal Function-Based Frequency Offset Design Based on Polynomial Fitting for Frequency Diverse Array Beampattern Synthesis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In the letter, a new frequency offset generation method based on polynomial fitting is proposed. The frequency offset can be obtained by sampling the fitted curve. By adjusting the coefficients of the polynomial, different forms of frequency offset can be generated. Different from existing window-based frequency diverse arrays (FDAs), which adopt traditional window functions to generate frequency offset and suffer from high sidelobe levels (SLLs) and low range resolution, the performance of Poly-FDA can be more flexibly regulated by fitting different forms of polynomial curves. Moreover, the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is exploited in the coefficient optimization process to obtain the optimal polynomial curve and enhanced beampattern property. Numerical examples demonstrate the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed Poly-FDA with lower SLL and narrower beamwidth other than the existing window-based FDAs and FDA of other frequency offset forms.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Sparse Arrays With Discrete Phase Constraints via Mixed-Integer Programming
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Synthesizing sparse arrays with discrete phase constraints is a critical problem in many applications. In this letter, we present a novel approach for synthesizing sparse arrays with discrete phase constraints using mixed-integer programming (MIP). The proposed approach optimizes both antenna positions and amplitude/phase excitations subject to the given discrete phase constraints. We show that our approach is flexible and can handle various practical constrains, such as minimum spacing constraints between elements, phase-only constraints in reconfigurable arrays. For each scenario, we obtain different MIP formulations, which can be solved using off-the-shelf solvers. Representative simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in sparse array synthesis.

articleTitle: Radiation Field Distribution Above Sea Surface of Underwater Microstrip Antenna Array
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Microstrip antenna has attracted extensive attention in the field of seafloor detection and underwater radar due to its stable structure and strong beam directivity. In this letter, the total-field scattered-field source finite-difference time-domain method with a simplified calculation method is considered to analyze the electromagnetic wave propagation generated by an underwater microstrip antenna (UMA). We analyze the field distributions of UMA, reduced-scale antenna and the two-element array composed of two UMAs. Meanwhile, the effect of element spacing on the radiation field distribution generated by the array is specifically studied. In addition, the scattering field of a metallic ellipsoidal target is analyzed. The simulations show that seawater can be used as the medium layer of the UMA in order to generate energy distribution in a near region similar to that of the conventional microstrip antenna. Furthermore, the element spacing for the underwater array should be adjusted based on the practical application.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Improvement for Patch Antenna via Knowledge-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, knowledge-based deep reinforcement learning (KBDRL) is used to improve patch antenna bandwidth. Conventional optimization algorithms usually require manual configuration of hyper-parameters of the algorithms, which cannot be learned automatically. In contrast, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) employs an end-to-end learning methodology that autonomously learns a policy to achieve optimal bandwidth. Additionally, it excels in efficiently handling nonlinear and nonconvex optimization problems. However, DRL consumes a lot of computing resources when there are many variables. To solve this problem, we propose a KBDRL approach that efficiently combines professional knowledge and machine learning methods. The proposed method is applied to a patch antenna with a size of 25 mm × 25 mm for which the obtained relative bandwidth is 39.18%. Our study shows that KBDRL has remarkable advantages compared to several commonly used local optimization algorithms, global optimization algorithms, and numerical optimization algorithms. Moreover, KBDRL can not only improve the performance of the antenna, but also explore the upper limitation of the performance with a finite-size basic structure.

Author Keywords: twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement in Arrow-Shaped Polarization Conversion Metasurface Under Seven Plasmonic Resonances
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An arrow-shaped unit cell formed polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) is further studied with enhanced polarization rotation (PR) bandwidth under seven resonances. The PCM covers 5.66–36.74 GHz (146.6%) PR bandwidth with a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) exceeding 90%. Comprehensive analysis of its ultrawideband characteristics, facilitated by multiple electric and magnetic resonances, is conducted through field distributions and equivalent circuits. A prototype of the PCM arranged in a chessboard configuration is simulated, fabricated, and measured to validate the analytical findings. The PCM prototype realizes a 10 dB monostatic radar cross section (RCS) across the frequency range of 5.5–37 GHz (148%) under both x- and y-polarized normal incident waves. The ultrathin wideband PCM is promising for applications in polarization converters and conformal RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Spurious-Free Characteristic Mode Formulation Based on Surface Integral Equation for N Lossy/Lossless Penetrable Objects and N PECs
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel surface integral equation (SIE)-based theory of characteristic modes (TCM) for arbitrarily shaped N lossy/lossless penetrable objects and N perfect electric conductors is proposed in this letter. Compared to previous work, the novel SIE-based generalized eigenvalue equation is valid for any number of objects and valid for objects that contact with each other by employing the contact-region modeling technique. Moreover, a novel combined field integral equation-based TCM has been proposed in this letter to deal with the internal resonance and decrease the condition numbers.

articleTitle: A Low RCS Wideband Antenna Based on Share-structure of FSA and ME-dipole
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A wideband integrated antenna is proposed with the realization of radiation and dual-polarized absorption in the same frequency band. The novelty of the proposed integrated structure lies in the share-aperture of the frequency-selective absorber and magnetoelectric dipole, which remain mutually independent and have orthogonal operating characteristics. In the share-structure, each array element can be selectively connected to an excitation port or a resistor loading (50 Ω) to reuse the antenna port impedance for receiving and absorbing copolarized waves. While the cross-polarized waves are reflected by antenna ground and absorbed by mounted resistors on the symmetric patches at the top layer of the antenna array. Consequently, the proposed antenna exhibits both wideband radiation and dual-polarized absorption simultaneously with a low profile (0.22λ0). Finally, a prototype 2 × 2 antenna array is fabricated and measured, demonstrating an impedance bandwidth of 92.7% for |S11| < −10 dB from 2.2 to 6 GHz. Moreover, the proposed antenna has 10 dB RCS reduction bandwidth of 100% (2–6 GHz) for x- and y-polarized normally incident waves.

articleTitle: Miniaturized FSS with Ultra-wide Out-of-band Suppression Based on Parallel-Plate Capacitor
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In order to solve the problem of poor ultrawide out-of-band suppression performance of existing filtennas. In this letter, a novel design method of miniaturized frequency selective surface (FSS) with ultrawide out-of-band suppression is investigated. Parallel-plate capacitor (PPC) structure is introduced into a basic nonresonant bandpass FSS to construct an equivalent series LC circuit with a low Q factor. The low-Q PPC resonator effectively increases suppression bandwidth by stronger interlayer coupling. The large value of PPC is also beneficial for the miniaturization and stability of passband. Finally, the unit size and thickness of the modified FSS are all reduced to 0.06λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (3 mm), which totally avoids the appearance of a grating lobe under 50 GHz. The −1 dB passband of our design is stable in 5.3 GHz to 7.4 GHz when the incident angle is up to 45° at both TE and TM polarizations. Simultaneously, the −20 dB suppression band covers 10 GHz to 45 GHz. The measured and simulated results validate great performance of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Research on the Propagation Characteristics of Power Exponential Vortex Beams in Hypersonic Plasma Turbulence
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) has a unique mode division multiplexing model that can increase the communication capacity and density of laser communication without increasing the frequency spectrum while achieving high-density and high-capacity laser communication and greatly improving transmission capacity. This letter conducts the model in hypersonic target plasma turbulence and investigates the OAM multiplexing characteristics in line-of-sight multiple-input–multiple-output systems under a plasma turbulence environment. The singular value (SV) and spectrum efficiency (SE) of power exponential vortex beams are compared with those of normal vortex beams. In addition, the intensity and phase of the power exponential vortex light penetrating turbulence are analyzed. Results show that the SE and SV of power exponential vortex beams are higher than those of ordinary vortex beams in hypersonic plasma turbulence under certain conditions. This finding indicates that the communication performance of power exponential vortex beams in plasma turbulence is better than that of ordinary vortex beams. These results can provide a theoretical basis for the analysis of hypersonic plasma targets.

articleTitle: Wideband Dual Circularly Polarized Substrate Integrated Cavity Antenna Array for Millimeterwave Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a novel design of a wideband dual circularly polarized (dual CP) substrate-integrated cavity (SIC) antenna array operating in millimeter-wave (MMW) bands. To realize <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathrm{T}{{\mathrm{M}}_{211}}$</tex-math></inline-formula> mode in the SIC and maintain it over a wide spectrum, a circular patch functioning as an electrical wall is loaded in the center of the aperture. The impedance matching can be improved by tuning the dimensions of the slots on the patch. For obtaining wideband dual circular polarizations, a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) sequential rotating (SR) network utilizing self-compensating phase shifters is designed. A 2 × 2 array prototype is fabricated and measured, which exhibits a wide impedance bandwidth of 33.4% and a wide axial ratio bandwidth of 33.8% for both polarizations, with a peak gain of 15.6 dBic. The satisfactory electromagnetic characteristic of the proposed antenna makes it suitable for scenarios with wide bandwidth and CP requirements in the millimeter-wave bands.

articleTitle: A 2-Bit Electronically Planar Reconfigurable Array Antenna With 2-D Beam-Scanning Capacity Using Hybrid Phase Control Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A 2-bit electronically planar reconfigurable array antenna (PRAA) at the Ku-band is presented in this letter. The proposed PRAA element employs the hybrid phase control method to realize the reconfiguration of its radiation structure and feeding structure. The radiation structure is designed as an O-slot radiation patch integrated with two p–i–n diodes to obtain a 1-bit phase quantization. To obtain the 2-bit phase control ability, a digital phase shifter with two p-i-n diodes is integrated into the feeding structure to obtain additional 90° phase shifting. Then, a 4 × 4-element subarray is designed and simulated, which is fed by using an asymmetric 16-way stripline feeding network. To realize 2-D beam scanning, an 8 × 8-element PRAA prototype is fabricated and measured, which is composed of four subarrays stitched together. The measured gain of the pencil beam is 20.8 dBi at 12.2 GHz with an aperture efficiency of 60.0%, while the 3 dB gain bandwidth is 13.9% (11.4–13.1 GHz). The measured results verify that the proposed PRAA has good 2-D beam scanning capability within ±45°. In addition, the height of the PPRA prototype is only 0.3λ0, which indicates this design has a highly integrated, planar, low-profile structure.

articleTitle: Broadband Metalized Plastic Waveguide Antenna with Robust Isolation Interface at 77 GHz
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A two-piece metallized plastic multichannel waveguide antenna comprising a novel high-isolation interface for automotive radar at 76 GHz to 81 GHz band is presented. The antenna contains three transmitters and four receivers. Each comprises a directive eight-horn linear array. All individual antenna elements are connected to the printed circuit board (PCB) through an innovative compressed waveguide interface combining 2-D polarization diversity and pseudoperiodic structures. A final prototype is fabricated employing injection molding, metallization, and soldering processes. Excellent performance is achieved, with a total efficiency up to 94% for channels from 76 GHz to 81 GHz, and an impedance bandwidth of 20.1%. Furthermore, the interface offers minimal coupling degradation over the antenna to PCB assembly tolerances. The design and fabrication method are an attractive alternative to conventional substrate-based antennas.

articleTitle: Direct Antenna Frequency-Hopped M-FSK Modulation With Time-Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: We present an innovative approach that simultaneously enables direct antenna frequency-hopped M-ary frequency shift keying (DAFH-MFSK) modulation and beamsteering through the use of time-modulated arrays (TMAs). The distinctive feature of our approach lies in the modulation of the TMA excitations with binary periodic sequences, which can be easily frequency-adjusted and time-delayed to simultaneously allow for DAFH-MFSK direct antenna modulation and beamsteering. Notably, our TMA proposal offers a distinct advantage over conventional architectures in terms of performance metrics, including reduced insertion losses and enhanced phase resolution for beamsteering, while also simplifying hardware complexity.

articleTitle: A Robust Low-Profile, Electrically Small, Unidirectional Mixed-Multipole Antenna Integrated With a Ground Surface
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: An innovative design of an electrically small, unidirectional mixed-multipole antenna (UMMA) compatible with a metal ground that has robust performance characteristics is developed for operation in the 915 MHz ISM-band. It incorporates both a ground-based magnetic near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) element and a driven composite electric element. The magnetic NFRP element is integrated into the ground surface. This arrangement increases the insensitivity of the UMMA to its presence. A prototype was fabricated and tested. The measured results, in good agreement with their simulated values, demonstrate that the UMMA is electrically small (ka = 0.96) and low-profile (0.038λ0). The robustness of the design is demonstrated with it maintaining its attractive broadside unidirectional performance when the UMMA is positioned arbitrarily on the ground for different sizes of that metal surface. The prototype's measured fractional bandwidth, peak realized gain, front-to-back ratio, and overall efficiency values are, respectively, 1.09%, 3.54 dBi, 15.26 dB, and 70.1%. Along with its wide beamwidth and simple low-cost realization, these properties are appealing to a variety of space-limited, narrow band, and low-power terminal devices and their applications.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband High-Efficiency Dual-Polarized Conformal Phase Array for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a novel methodology to remove the common-mode resonance of tightly coupled arrays using two-set unit cells and conformal operation is presented, whereby the ultrawideband dual-polarized conformal phase array is developed with high efficiency for wireless power transfer applications. Initially, a design method to shift the common-mode resonance of a tightly coupled array outside of the operating band using a two-set unit cell and conformal operation is described, and a dual-polarized two-set unit cell of infinite array is proposed with ultrawideband operation. Subsequently, the 8 × 8 dual-polarized two-set unit cells are designed to conform a cylindrical surface with a radius of 200 mm (1.3λ), resulting in a cylindrical-conformal tightly coupled array. Ultimately, an experimental prototype of the obtained conformal array was manufactured and measured. It achieves an operated bandwidth of 2.2∼12.4 GHz (5.6:1) with active VSWRs < 3.0 within ±60° scanning range in E-/H-planes and the average efficiency > 70% for dual-polarized operation. The good correspondence between the measured results and the simulated results illustrates the feasibility of the presented conformal array. Such a balanced, high-performance conformal phase array provides a perfect solution for wireless power transfer systems of various maneuverable platforms.

articleTitle: A Novel Mixed-Potential Integral Equation-Based Sub-Structure Characteristic-Mode Formulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel mixed-potential integral equation (MPIE)-based sub-structure generalized eigenvalue equation (SSGEE) for multilayer structure is proposed in this letter. Compared to state-of-the-art sub-structure characteristic mode (CM) formulations based on electromagnetic field integral formulation, the proposed MPIE-based SSGEE significantly reduces computation time and computer memory required. In addition, the proposed MPIE-based SSGEE can also be applied on different parts of a single object, which is well suited for obtaining the radiation characteristic of every radiator in the multiradiator system.

articleTitle: A Method of Dual-Bias Voltage Supply for Reducing Reflection Loss in Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces of Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we proposed a new method of dual-bias voltage supply for reducing reflection loss (RL) in reconfigurable intelligent surfaces of liquid crystal (RIS-LC). By independently controlling the resonances of two dipoles biased by two different voltages, a one-to-multiple correspondence between reflection phase and magnitude is established. Consequently, the RL can be minimized by selecting the optimal reflection magnitude for each reflection phase. For demonstration, a 12 × 13 array of RIS-LC is fabricated and measured. The experimental results show that the proposed RIS-LC achieves a maximum reflection magnitude of −0.7 dB with a reflection phase range of 570° at 41 GHz. It validates the proposed method can significantly reduce the RL without sacrificing reflection phase range. The presented RIS-LC possesses the advantages of simple structure, low cost, and ease of fabrication.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Broadband Circularly Polarized Stacked Patch Antenna Formed by Meshed Aluminum Disks for Inter-Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A broadband lightweight circularly polarized (CP) stacked patch antenna is proposed for use in the 1.8–2.3 GHz LEO-to-GEO inter-satellite links. It consists of four meshed aluminum disks supported by polyamide spacers. No dielectric substrate is used in the design to avoid heat storage in the substrate and reduce antenna weight. Thanks to the meshed structure, the antenna weight is reduced by half and is only 30 g. The broadband CP radiation is achieved via the sequential rotation feeding structure and the stacked patch topology. For verification, a prototype antenna is built and tested. In addition to the agreement between the simulated and measured results, the prototype antenna exhibits an overlapped 10 dB return loss and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 33.81% and in-band realized gain of 8.4–9.3 dBic at broadside, meeting the requirements of the intended inter-satellite link application.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized, Notched Electromagnetic Energy Harvester Array Based on FSS
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a dual-polarized, notched ambient electromagnetic (EM) energy harvester array based on frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented. The proposed unit structure consists of a notched solid patch with two through-vias. By introducing the notches into the solid patch, the current aggregation at the through-vias is enhanced. As a result, the EM energy flow is constrained, and high harvesting efficiency is achieved. Then, a 9 × 9 harvester array was fabricated and measured. Simulated and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed harvester features dual-polarization and wide-angle insensitive characteristics. At a 60° incidence angle of both TE and TM polarization, the harvesting efficiency exceeds 78%. Also, the half-power bandwidth maintains above 100 MHz, which covers the WiFi-band. Besides, it is also shown that the notched harvester has a small operating frequency offset of 30 MHz (1.23%). The proposed harvester can be used to construct a high-efficiency EM energy harvesting system for the wireless power supply of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual-Polarized Active Phased Array Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel miniaturized millimeter-wave (mmWave) dual-polarized (DP) active phased array antenna is proposed for the fifth generation (5G) application in this letter. The slotted patch antenna element only occupies 4 × 4 mm2 with a −10 dB |S11| bandwidth from 24.25 to 29.5 GHz. Four quasi-monopoles are added for wider bandwidth and beamwidth realization. Defective ground structure technology is adopted to remove the scanning blind spot. Using the DP eight-channel beamformer chips and multilayer printed circuit board technology, an active 8 × 8 phased array is designed, fabricated, and measured. Measured results show that the proposed antenna array can steer up to ±50° with a cross-polarization level lower than 22 dB. In summary, this phased array can be a good choice for 5G mmWave application considering the miniaturized, low-profile, wide bandwidth, and compact characterisitic.

articleTitle: An Optimization Approach Based on Separated Latent Space for Inverse Design of Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we propose an inverse design framework of electromagnetic metasurfaces (EMMSs) realized by optimizing latent variables in a separated latent space. In the training phase, the framework sequentially connects an inverse network to generate the shapes of scatterers by the input of reflection coefficients and a forward network to recover the coefficients with the generated scatterers. The architecture of the generative network adopted the fundamental structure of variational autoencoder, but the latent space was split into four subspaces representing the predefined classes of metasurfaces by applying multivariate normal distribution. After model training, for the inverse design of EMMSs, the generator of the inverse model and the decoder of the forward model are linked to an optimizer. This network pipeline enabled to build more streamlined inverse design model, and on the other hand the optimization strategy in the separated latent spaces improved the prediction accuracy of EMMSs concerning desired electromagnetic (EM) properties reducing the misfit rate by 31.9% compared with the counterpart method having a single distribution latent space.

articleTitle: Stored Energies and Q-Factor Expressed in Material Derivatives
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Stored energies of radiating systems have generated research interest for several decades due to their relationship with Q-factor and fractional bandwidth. In this letter, material derivatives are used to provide a new interpretation of widely used stored energy expressions. This provides a fundamental relationship between stored energies of radiating systems and their electromagnetic material properties. It is shown that electric stored energy is related to the electric material parameter (permittivity) derivative. Similarly, magnetic stored energy is linked to the derivative of the permeability. Furthermore, as an extension, Cauchy–Riemann equations are used to relate stored energy to dissipation.

articleTitle: Localization of the Radiated-PIM Source Based on the Truncated Time Reversal Operator-MUSIC Imaging: An Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The accurate localization of the radiated passive intermodulation (R-PIM) source generated inside the phased array has become an increasingly critical issue in guaranteeing the high communication quality of wireless communication systems. Due to the characteristic of spatial-temporal focusing, time reversal (TR) imaging is a promising solution for locating the R-PIM source in complex structures and complicated environments, which is yet always analyzed through numerical simulations. This letter develops the truncated TR operator multiple signals classification (TTRO-MUSIC) imaging method for accurate experimental localization of the R-PIM source. In the experimental platform of locating the R-PIM sources using TTRO-MUSIC, the R-PIM source is imitated by the sleeve antenna and placed inside the semi-closed metal cavity. The experimental results show that the positioning error of 0.12 wavelengths can be obtained by TTRO-MUSIC, and additional perturbations only raise the positioning error to 0.14 wavelengths. Compared to the 0.07 wavelengths obtained by the full-wave simulation, the ability to accurately locate the R-PIM source using TTRO-MUSIC has been validated because the intrinsic perturbations in the experimental data are considered.

articleTitle: High Isolation Dual-Polarized SISL Antenna with Out-of-Band Rejection Improvement Using Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter proposes a dual-polarized differential-fed substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) patch antenna with an out-of-band rejection level using an artificial magnetic conductor structure. By etching vertical and horizontal symmetrical slots A on an electromagnetically-coupled square patch antenna with vias connecting patch and feeding line to help the slots maintain good filtering selectivity, an additional resonance (fr2) is excited with lower radiation null (fn1) and the cancellation of the horizontal current on the radiating patch generated upper radiation null (fn2). On the other hand, a stacked patch provides upper radiation nulls fn3, and a 4 × 4 artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structure further enhances the antenna's rejection level at the upper band edge. The simulated and measured results show that an impedance bandwidth of 21.9% (2.93 GHz to 3.65 GHz) is achieved with a compact size of 0.55λ0 × 0.55λ0 × 0.06λ0 ( λ0 is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency). An out-of-band rejection level higher than 17.2 dB and 28.2 dB is obtained at lower and upper bands, respectively, with a maximum gain of approximately 8.2 dBi, and stable radiation patterns are realized within the passband.

articleTitle: Ultrathin Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a dual-band circularly polarized microstrip antenna with an ultrathin substrate made of liquid crystal polymer (LCP). The proposed antenna consists of a gridded patch and a round of via fence for dual-band radiation and size miniaturization. Compared with the previous designs, the proposed antenna has two improvements in structures with merits: first, a parasitic patch is added below the gridded patch to tune the ratio of dual-band frequencies; second, a stacked feeding network with dual orthogonal L-shaped probes is designed for profile reduction, also providing the feasibility of differential feed and dual-linear polarization. Based on the codesign of the gridded patch, the parasitic patch, and the stacked feeding network, all layers of the antenna are clamped into a flexible board with an ultrathin thickness of 0.6 mm (0.013λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at 6.5 GHz) and taped out with the flexible LCP process. The measured results show the bandwidths of total efficiency over 25% are 6.25–6.74 GHz and 7.92–8.17 GHz with circular polarization, proving to be a feasible solution for flexible antennas in space-limited mobile handsets.

articleTitle: A Simple Polarization-Reconfigurable Series-Fed Patch Array Using Switchable Feeding Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we presents a polarization-reconfigurable series-fed patch antenna with high gain and a simple switching mechanism. The proposed design comprises of four slotted circular patches arranged in a 1 × 4 configuration. For excitation, the array is capacitive fed by a single T-junction power divider.   By controlling the bias state of three p-i-n diodes on the divider, the antenna's polarization can be switched among a single linear and dual-sense circular polarization. To validate the design concept, an array prototype is fabricated and measured at the operating frequency of 5.0 GHz. The measurements result in a common operating bandwidth for all radiating modes of about 1.8%, ranging from 4.95 GHz to 5.04 GHz. Besides, a stable broadside gain of around 12 dBi is also obtained.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Path Loss Modeling with Simplified Features
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Propagation modeling is a crucial tool for successful wireless deployments and spectrum planning with the demand for high modeling accuracy continuing to grow. Recognizing that detailed knowledge of the physical environment (terrain and clutter) is essential, we propose a novel approach that uses environmental information for predictions. Instead of relying on complex, detail-intensive models, we explore the use of simplified scalar features involving the total obstruction depth along the direct path from transmitter to receiver. Obstacle depth offers a streamlined, yet surprisingly accurate, method for predicting wireless signal propagation, providing a practical solution for efficient and effective wireless network planning.

articleTitle: A Novel Procedure To Hybridize The Folded Transmitarray and Fabry Perot Cavity With Low Antenna Profile and Flexible Design Frequency
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The previously reported procedure to hybridize the high-band folded transmitarray antenna (FTA) and the low-band Fabry-Perot-cavity-antenna (FPCA) adopts the λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>/2 FPCA as the basic antenna, and the FTA is then integrated with the FPCA. The aperture size and profile of the implemented antenna are highly correlated to the λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>, which restricts further profile shrunk and designable λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> under a given aperture size. A novel procedure tackling these issues is proposed. A double-folded FTA (DFFTA) whose profile is 1/4 of the focal length is first adopted as the basic antenna under a given aperture size. Then, an FPCA with an artificial magnetic conductor-loaded ground is integrated with the DFFTA. The aperture size and the profile of the implemented antenna are completely determined by the DFFTA, which has no correlations of the λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>. An aperture-shared dual-band antenna with a lower profile at both operating bands can be designed by this procedure. Further, the λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub> can be freely chosen under a given aperture size and profile. An aperture-shared surface offering partial reflection at 3.5 GHz and phase correction at 28 GHz, and an aperture-shared multifunctional ground offering polarization conversion at 28 GHz and phase compensation at 3.5 GHz are proposed to execute the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Broadband Mutual Coupling Reduction of Multiple Electrical-Current Nulls for Quad-Port Shared-Radiator Slot Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel quad-port shared-radiator slot antenna with broadband decoupling characteristics is proposed. The proposed slot antenna (PSA) has multiple electrical-current nulls for decoupling, formed by the cancellation of contrary characteristic modes (CMs) currents. The reduction of broadband mutual coupling can be achieved by changing the slot width at the four edges and corners of the original slot antenna (OSA). The −10 dB operating bandwidth is expanded from 28.6% on OSA to 69.7% on PSA. The isolations are only 7–9 dB on OSA but improved to better than 17 dB on PSA, even reaching a maximum of 25 dB. The total efficiency of PSA has a significant improvement compared to the OSA, and the envelope correlation coefficients of PSA are close to zero, far below the OSA. The good coincidence between the simulated and measured results confirms the correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Integrated Microwave and Millimeter-Wave Circularly Polarized Antenna with ISM Band Gain Suppression Performance
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, an integrated microwave and millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) dual-band circularly polarized (CP) antenna using the structural reuse method is proposed. The mm-Wave CP antenna is a 2 × 2 array employing the sequential rotated array technique, in which the CP radiating element is constructed using two centrally symmetrical L-shaped patches that are excited via a substrate-integrated coaxial line (SICL) feeding network. In terms of the microwave CP antenna, a slot-coupled square patch fed through a microstrip directional coupler incorporating stubs is developed. One microstrip stub is added to introduce a new coupling path with an opposite current, thus forming an additional null in the upper sideband. The measured results demonstrate that the proposed CP antenna exhibits impressive impedance bandwidths of 27.91% [(2.24 to 2.91) GHz] in the microwave band and 23.53% [(24.45 to 31.04) GHz] in the mm-Wave band, respectively. The remarkable isolation between the two operating bands (over 45 dB) ensures independent operation. Moreover, the antenna demonstrates a notable out-of-band suppression level of 33 dB in the industrial scientific medical band, indicating favorable gain filtering characteristics.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna for WLAN/UWB Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel ultrawideband (UWB) dual-polarized omnidirectional antenna with a low profile has been proposed for wireless local area networks (WLAN) and UWB applications. The antenna is comprised of two components: a vertically polarized (VP) sheet-like tapered monopole and a horizontally polarized (HP) tightly coupled circular connected array with Vivaldi antennas. The HP structure functions as the metal ground of the VP structure to overcome match deterioration when the HP structure is placed near the metal ground of the VP structure. This design results in a low profile of only 0.08λmin for the dual-polarized antenna (λmin represents the wavelength at the lowest frequency within the working band). The antenna provides an overlapped bandwidth of 2.4–10.6 GHz (126%) and an isolation greater than 20 dB within the band. Meanwhile, high efficiency and uniform omnidirectional radiation patterns with a gain variation of less than 3 dB in the horizontal plane are obtained. These appealing properties enable the antenna an ideal choice for UWB applications and wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna with Traveling Wave Loop
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel ultrawideband circularly polarized crossed dipole antenna is introduced in this letter. The proposed structure consists of two pairs of octagonal crossed dipoles, four parasitic patches, a parasitic traveling-wave circular loop and 12 vertical grounded metal sheets. The design incorporates parasitic closed circular loops and vertical grounded metal sheets to enhance the impedance bandwidth (IBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW), particularly at lower frequencies. In addition, theoretical analysis of the radiation characteristics of the traveling-wave loop is also provided for comprehension. The measured results of prototype are in good agreement with the simulated results. The measured IBW (<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$|S_{11}|<$</tex-math></inline-formula> −10 dB) is from 1.13 to 3.83 GHz (108.9<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>) and the ARBW (AR<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$<$</tex-math></inline-formula> 3 dB) is from 1.18 to 3.82 GHz (105.6<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>). Furthermore, the antenna exhibits a wideband 3 dB antenna gain bandwidth from 1.1 to 3.95 GHz (112.9<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>)

articleTitle: Design of a Compact and Wideband Printed Monopole Antenna With Stable Omnidirectional Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel printed monopole antenna is proposed in this letter, which is composed of a monopole radiator and a feeding structure. The proposed feeding structure along the feed line, consisting of a metasurface and two arms, can regulate the surface currents on the ground to stabilize the radiation pattern and adjust the impedance matching of the radiator, respectively. Consequently, a broad operating bandwidth can be achieved due to these combined structures. A prototype is fabricated based on this design, and a wide bandwidth of 0.95–5.2 GHz for |S11| < −10 dB is observed. The planar dimension of this prototype is 0.3λmax(95 mm) × 0.046λmax(15 mm), where λmax is the wavelength corresponding to the lowest operating frequency. The measured peak realized gain ranges from 0.8 to 5.7 dBi, and a stable omnidirectional radiation pattern is observed across its operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Circularly Polarized Reconfigurable Capacitance-Loaded Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A novel miniaturized circularly polarized (CP) capacitance-loaded patch antenna with a simple structure and frequency reconfigurability is proposed in this letter. Unlike the conventional half-wavelength patch antenna, the proposed antenna has a cavity-like structure and, hence, does not require a large ground plane to achieve low back-lobe levels. It utilizes capacitance loading, which significantly reduces the size of the antenna in communication devices and systems. To achieve frequency reconfigurability, a pair of orthogonal radiation gaps (equivalent resonance capacitance) are tuned by introducing two varactors. A tuning range from 880 to 947 MHz is achieved by varying the bias voltages. Good −10 dB impedance and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidths are observed at each operating frequency in the tuning range. The reconfigurable antenna gain is between 4.4 and 4.8 dBic. The remarkable advantages of the proposed antenna make it a potential candidate for Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: A New Sigmoidal Transformation for Strongly Near-Singular Integrals Over Triangular Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A sigmoidal transformation is applied to the singularity cancellation method to improve the numerical integration accuracy of strongly near-singular integrals over triangular elements. By employing the sigmoidal transformation, the quadrature points near to and distant from the singularity can both be redistributed to carry more information of the integrand. Improved accuracy and error convergence of typical strongly near-singular integrals are observed. To further increase the manipulation flexibility of the quadrature points, a new sigmoidal transformation is proposed in this letter. Several numerical results are presented to show the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A High-gain Fabry-Perot Resonator Antenna With Dual-sense Circular Polarization Diversity
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In the letter, a broadband circularly polarized (CP) Fabry–Perot (FP) resonator antenna with both high gain and polarization diversity is proposed for satellite communications. A single-layer partially reflective surface (PRS) is employed to be positioned over a planar metallic ground, thus creating an air-filled FP cavity. The PRS layer is designed to exhibit a positively sloped reflection phase and a large reflection magnitude, which is beneficial to extend the 3 dB gain bandwidth of the FP antenna. In addition, a more closed FP cavity is formed by surrounding the ground with four vertically orientated metal sheets, which can further improve the FP antenna's gain. A slot-coupled patch antenna is utilized as the primary source of the FP cavity. To enable the antenna to switch between the dual-sense circular polarization modes, a feeding network composed of a Wilkinson power divider and a reconfigurable <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${\text{90}}^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula> phase shifter is designed. To verify the concept, the proposed FP antenna was fabricated and tested. Experimental results demonstrate that the FP antenna shows an axial ratio of less than 3 dB and a return loss exceeding 10 dB across the frequency bands of (5.18 to 5.78) GHz and (5.34 to 5.7) GHz for left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) and right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) modes, respectively. It also obtains good radiation patterns with high front-to-back ratios and low cross polarizations for both CP operations. Furthermore, the antenna realizes consistent gains, ranging from 12 dBic to 14.9 dBic for LHCP mode and 12.4 dBic to 14.3 dBic for RHCP mode in the band of operation.

articleTitle: Minimum Spatial Sampling Method Under Spherical Test Zone in MIMO OTA Testing
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a novel 3-D test zone sampling method is proposed to realize efficient dynamic channel emulation in multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) over-the-air (OTA) testing. By characterizing the spatial correlation with Fourier expansion, this method can derive the minimum necessary number of test zone samples for high fidelity channel emulation. This approach significantly reduces the complexity associated with probe weight computation, which is essential for dynamic channel emulation. The simulation results indicate that compared with the sampling method with <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{\mathbf{0.1}}}$</tex-math></inline-formula> wavelength interval, the proposed method reduces spatial samples of virtual antennas to <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${{\mathbf{53.4}}\%}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, which is significant for MIMO OTA testing.

articleTitle: Short-range MIMO Throughput Prediction based on Spherical Wave Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: The exploration of Internet-of-Things (IoT) has led to widespread short-range multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) communications. However, traditional throughput models, limited by the far-field propagation assumptions, often fail to accurately evaluate the spatial multiplexing capability and throughput performance in short-range line-of-sight (LOS) scenarios. Against this backdrop, this letter reveals the limitations of the conventional plane wave model-based throughput model from the perspective of the effective degree of freedom (EDOF) and develops a MIMO throughput model for short-range LOS scenarios using a spherical wave model (SWM). The relationship between EDOF and throughput is analyzed and discussed. Our results show that EDOF can effectively indicate throughput variations across different transceiver layouts in short-range LOS scenarios. Throughput measurements of MIMO devices are conducted to show the superiority of the proposed SWM-based throughput model to the traditional one.

articleTitle: A Compact Circularly Polarized Filtering Dipole Antenna with Co-layered Printed Ring Structures
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter presents a simple structure wideband circularly polarized (CP) dipole antenna with bandpass-type filtering radiation response. It consists of a cross-dipole radiator with the arms printed on both the top and bottom sides of the substrate. Four pairs of rotated metal strips and a compact square ring structure are coupled to the arms to enhance the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth. In order to realize bandpass-type filtering radiation response, two rectangular rings are introduced to generate two specific radiation nulls, ensuring high-frequency selectivity at operating band edges. To obtain compact size and avoid intersection with the dipole arms, the two ring structures are printed on the top and bottom sides of the substrate using the metallic jumper vias. This wideband CP filtering dipole antenna is implemented and tested. The antenna oversize is 0.8λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.8λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.17λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The measured results show that the proposed antenna has an overlap impedance and AR bandwidth of 14.1%. A stable realized gain of about 7.2 dBic and two radiation nulls are obtained without using extra filter circuits.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna With Novel Asymmetric Y-Shaped Arms
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized antenna with novel asymmetric Y-shaped parasitic arms is proposed. The antenna consists of Y-shaped feedlines with vacant-quarter rings, asymmetric Y-shaped parasitic arms, rectangular patches, and a reflector. The circularly polarized radiation is generated by exciting the Y-shaped feedlines with vacant-quarter rings. The impedance matching bandwidth (IBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) are effectively improved by introducing asymmetric Y-shaped parasitic arms, and four CP modes are introduced in the operating band. The overall dimensions of the proposed antenna are 0.84λ0×0.84λ0×0.27λ0 (λ0 is the wavelength of the center frequency in the free space), with a simple structure. The measured results show that the wide IBW covers 1.2–3.0 GHz (86%), and the ARBW is 1.3–3.2 GHz (84%). Moreover, 79% of the overlap bandwidth (1.32–3.0 GHz) is achieved between IBW and ARBW, and the measured cross-polarization discrimination is more than 18 dBic on the Z-axis. The antenna can be used in wireless communication due to the characteristics of wide impedance bandwidth and axial ratio bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Deployable Coplanar Waveguide CoCo Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a deployable coplanar waveguide (CPW) coaxial colinear (CoCo) antenna is proposed with full coverage in the H-plane. The antenna features an ultra-thin profile of only 0.1 mm with excellent deployability. The proposed antenna consists of eight units, which are connected through metal crossover lines. The top and bottom metal layers alternate as the inner and outer conductors of the CPW. Metal bridges are introduced to mitigate the open stopband (OSB) phenomenon, which also eliminates the undesired CPW slot mode. A planar choke is designed to eliminate the effects of unbalanced coaxial feeding, ensuring consistency between the measured and simulated results. The antenna was fabricated using flexible printed circuit (FPC) technology. Within the target 4.8 GHz to 4.9 GHz band, the measured S11 is below −10 dB, and the efficiency is about 80%. The average gain in the H-plane is 5.8 dBi. The antenna shows great potential for applications in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other mobile communication devices.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Monolithic Thinned Dielectric Superstrate for Performance Enhancement in DRAA
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, an innovative methodology is presented for the design of a monolithic thinned dielectric superstrate (TDS) aimed at enhancing the gain and minimizing the sidelobe levels (SLLs) associated with dielectric resonator antenna arrays (DRAAs). A novel configuration of the monolithic TDS is meticulously analyzed and subsequently integrated with a 1 × 2 element DRAA operating in the C-band spectrum. This integration is primarily done to align the radiated electric fields (EFs) phase, which culminates in enhanced antenna characteristics. The design and optimization of the proposed TDS are systematically executed using the differential evolution algorithm, specifically utilizing the thinning technique. Electromagnetic (EM) simulations and measurement studies are performed to elucidate the efficacy of the developed methodology. Preliminary findings from the EM simulations indicate that introducing the proposed TDS yields a significant performance enhancement. To be precise, the superstrate enables a gain enhancement of 4 dBi and an SLL decrement of 5 dB over a frequency bandwidth of 300 MHz relative to configurations devoid of the superstrate. Significantly, the observed measurements validate the proposed design strategy, aligning well with simulation results and confirming its practical efficacy and viability. In essence, this innovative design offers a notable enhancement in DRAA performance without necessitating any escalation in design complexity or spatial dimensions.

articleTitle: Simulation of X-Rays Effect on Cavity Filters Based on SO-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Radiation interference on electronic devices is not negligible, and it is very important to analyze the causes of interference and the impact it has. This letter investigates the effect of X-rays on the output frequency of metal cavity filters. X-rays can generate primary and secondary electrons in the filter cavity. These electrons together form a plasma that affects the transmission characteristics of the electromagnetic wave, and thus interferes with the operation of the filter. To investigate this phenomenon, first a geometric modeling of 3-D metal cavity filter filled with plasma is constructed; then it is converted into a computable electromagnetic model of time domain finite difference (FDTD). Second, the electromagnetic wave transmission in the filter after exposure to X-ray radiation is calculated using the shift operator-FDTD method. Finally, after simulating the transmission characteristics, the results indicate that at different moments (1–3.5 ns) and at different air pressures (0.2 and 0.3 Torr), the frequency selection characteristics of the metal cavity filter change significantly, and the signal is even completely cut off in severe cases, which provides a reference for the performance of electronic devices within ionizing radiation environments.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Design of Orbital Angular Momentum Generators by Leaky-Wave Holograms
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces a pioneering approach for the design of holographic leaky-wave antennas, effectively generating electromagnetic waves carrying orbital angular momentum by synergizing flat optics and deep learning (DL) techniques. In this study, we employ the DL technique to tune the constituent parameters of the hologram surface impedance, uncovering a framework adept at controlling radiation pattern characteristics. By utilizing a total of 77 000 generated datasets, we deduce the optimal values for each parameter, resulting in the attainment of the desired radiation pattern. Importantly, the utilization of DL not only accelerates the process but also yields outcomes of greater accuracy compared to manual parameter adjustments and conventional optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Tripolarized Antenna With High Isolation and Diverse Patterns
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, a high-isolation wideband tripolarized antenna with broadside and monopole-like radiation patterns is proposed. It consists of a four-element circular loop array and two orthogonally-positioned dipoles. The crossed dipoles generate <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\pm \text{45}^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula> linearly polarized (LP) broadside radiations while the vertically LP omnidirectional patterns are produced by the loop array. To lower the operating frequencies and simultaneously expand the bandwidth, four groups of slots are first introduced in the <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\Gamma$</tex-math></inline-formula>-shaped Balun design and second four narrow circular ring strips are added to arms of dipoles. For verification, a tripolarized antenna was fabricated and measured. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed antenna obtains a wide overlapped band operating from 3.5 to 5.4 GHz with port-to-port isolation higher than 30 dB in most of the band. Directional and symmetrical patterns are attained for the dipoles and also the omnidirectional radiation patterns are maintained for the vertically polarized loop array across the entire band. Furthermore, the antenna yields measured peak gains of 8.8, 8.2, and 6.9 dBi in two broadside modes and monopole-like mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Bifunctional Water-Based Frequency-Selective Absorber Regulated by Gravity Field
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A bifunctional water-based frequency-selective absorber (FSA) regulated by gravity field realizing the functions of absorptive frequency-selective transmission (AFST) structure and absorptive frequency-selective reflection (AFSR) structure is proposed. The device is made up of two containers with distinct shapes that are connected by locating cylinders. The lossless layer utilizes a bandpass frequency-selective surface with a cross gap. Gravity will shape the water into blocks when the AFST structure is pointed toward the Earth. It is demonstrated that the AFST state obtains a transmission coefficient greater than −3 dB from 2.85 to 4.48 GHz, with an 80% absorptive band from 5.02 to 20 GHz. When the device is turned upside down, the AFSR structure fills with water, making the water shaped like grids. In this state, the device acquires a −3 dB reflection band from 2.42 to 7.78 GHz and an 80% absorption band from 9.66 to 20 GHz. Two equivalent circuit models are proposed to provide insight into the operation mechanism of the FSA. A prototype of the proposed FSA is fabricated and measured to verify its performance. The proposed bifunctional FSA is expected to be used in ground-to-air antijamming communication.

articleTitle: Compact Absorptive Dual-Beam Patch Antenna by Fusing Resistor-Terminated Defected Microstrip Structure
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A compact absorptive dual-beam patch antenna is proposed by fusing the absorptive branch inside the patch antenna. The defected microstrip structure with a meander slot and the T-shaped shorted stub can make the absorptive branch achieve the absorptive function in a small size so that it can be fused into the dumbbell-shaped slot of the patch antenna. Furthermore, the dumbbell-shaped slot extends the current path of the patch operating at TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> mode. Thus, the overall size of the patch antenna doesnot increase but decreases. Compared with other absorptive antennas, the proposed one realizes the out-of-band reflectionless characteristic in a compact size and dual-beam radiation. For demonstration, a prototype operated at 5.8 GHz was measured with the compact size of 0.31λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.48λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, the out-of-band reflectionless bandwidth of 49.5% (3.50–5.72 GHz and 6.46–7.11 GHz), and the dual radiation beams directed at ±42°.

articleTitle: Empirical Formulas for Superdirectivities of Broadside Linear and Square Arrays
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: Empirical formulas are proposed for the superdirectivities of broadside linear and square arrays. The formulas are derived based on a large amount of numerical results of optimum directivity for the superdirectivity of a broadside linear array of isotropic elements with an electrical element spacing varying from 0 to 0.5. The formulas for the linear array can also be developed for the square array. Besides the isotropic elements, the superdirectivity of the square array of different unidirectional elements is also numerically analyzed. It is found that the square array of unidirectional elements offers higher directivity than that of isotropic elements for a small number of elements, but tends to consistency as the element number increases. The numerical results are validated with the full-wave simulation of a square array of planar inverted-F antennas, considering coupling effects between elements.

articleTitle: Single-Channel Imaging at Low Sampling Rates
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: This letter introduces a method for single-channel imaging at low sampling rates, utilizing frequency-modulated continuous wave radar combined with space–frequency multiplexing. This approach significantly reduces system complexity and data acquisition demands by encoding scene reflectivity into a single, low-frequency signal. A mathematical framework supporting this technique is developed and followed by an experimental demonstration, where an image is reconstructed using a transmit antenna and a 15-element receive array within the (92 GHz to 96 GHz) band, whose interaction is converted into a single beat signal with a 32 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Wide Impedance-Bandwidth Microstrip Comb-Line Array Antenna Using High Sidelobe Suppression Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: In this letter, we introduce a wide impedance bandwidth microstrip comb-line array antenna in the millimeter-wave band. To achieve wide impedance bandwidth performance, a series-fed array antenna consisting of three types of radiating structures is designed on a substrate utilizing printed circuit board technology. Different from the traditional comb-line array, parasitic components are introduced in the vicinity of the radiating elements to obtain low sidelobe levels (SLLs). The antenna is constructed and measured to confirm its viability. The measured impedance bandwidth (voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR) <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\leq$</tex-math></inline-formula> 2) is 30.02% (20.1 GHz to 27.2 GHz) with satisfactory impedance matching. Meanwhile, the SLL of the comb antenna is about −22 dB at 26.6 GHz. Therefore, the proposed antenna boasts advantages including a simple manufacturing process with low fabrication cost, ease of integration, wide impedance bandwidth, and low sidelobes.

articleTitle: Shared Dipoles Inspired Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna with Broad Bandwidth
publicationTitle: IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters
abstract: A horizontal-polarized (HP) omnidirectional antenna with an extremely wide bandwidth and small gain variation is presented. To attain horizontally polarized omnidirectional performance and small size, eight shared dipoles, which are round-connected into an octagon-shaped array, are excited by a 1-to-8 power divider. To significantly improve the impedance matching and omnidirectional performance over a very broad operating frequency band, fragmented metal strips are introduced around the shared dipoles.
